493	    func hideSilentSection() -> InspectorSection {
494	        let binding = self.binding
495	        let name = "Hide While Silent"
496	        /// The sentence of the last refused `ops(forMedia:)`, shown as the note.
497	        final class Problem { var text: String? }

499	        func candidates() -> [MediaSnapshot] {

501	        }
502	        func gated() -> [ClipSnapshot] { binding.videoClips.filter { $0.video?.hideSilent != nil } }
503	        func anyOn() -> Bool { !gated().isEmpty }

508	        /// The media's `set_media_speech` ops, or nil when `ops(forMedia:)`
509	        /// refused: then the row writes nothing and the note says why.
510	        func spans(_ media: UInt32) -> [ReelOp]? {
511	            do {
512	                let ops = try DuckSpeech.ops(
513	                    forMedia: media, in: binding.snapshot,
514	                    cacheDirectory: binding.document?.cacheDirectory)
515	                problem.text = nil
516	                return ops
517	            } catch {
518	                problem.text = error.localizedDescription
519	                return nil
520	            }
521	        }
522	        /// The whole gate `next` on every selected picture clip, the spans first.
523	        func write(_ next: HideSilentProps) -> [ReelOp] {
524	            guard let speech = spans(next.media) else { return [] }
525	            return speech + binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(hideSilent: .some(next)))
526	        }
527	        func onOps() -> [ReelOp] {
528	            guard let first = candidates().first else { return [] }
529	            let gate = HideSilentProps(media: first.id)
530	            let set = binding.videoClips.filter { $0.video?.hideSilent == nil }.flatMap {
531	                binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(hideSilent: .some(gate)), for: $0)
532	            }
533	            guard !set.isEmpty, let speech = spans(gate.media) else { return [] }
534	            return speech + set
535	        }
536	        func offOps() -> [ReelOp] { binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(hideSilent: .some(nil))) }
537	        func offerable() -> Bool {
538	            guard let first = candidates().first else { return false }
539	            return DuckSpeech.problem(
540	                forMedia: first.id, in: binding.snapshot,
541	                cacheDirectory: binding.document?.cacheDirectory) == nil
542	        }
543	        /// "Speech from"'s media: the candidates, then the set media when it
544	        /// is not among them.

546	            var list = candidates()
547	            if let set = current()?.media, !list.contains(where: { $0.id == set }),
548	               let row = binding.snapshot.media(set)
549	            {
550	                list.append(row)
551	            }
552	            return list
553	        }
554	        let sourceList = sources()
555	        func seconds(_ ticks: Ticks) -> Double { ReelTime.seconds(ticks) }
556	        func ticks(_ seconds: Double) -> Ticks { ReelTime.ticks(seconds: max(seconds, 0)) }
557	        func edit(_ change: (inout HideSilentProps) -> Void) -> [ReelOp] {
558	            guard var next = current() else { return [] }
559	            change(&next)
560	            return write(next)
561	        }
562	
563	        let check = OptionCheckboxControl(
564	            label: "Hide while silent", read: allOn,
565	            write: { value in binding.apply(name, value ? onOps() : offOps()) },
566	            enabled: { anyOn() || offerable() }, onEdit: { binding.edited() })
567	        if !anyOn(), let first = candidates().first {

569	                forMedia: first.id, in: binding.snapshot,
570	                cacheDirectory: binding.document?.cacheDirectory)
571	        } else if candidates().isEmpty, !anyOn() {
572	            check.toolTip = "No clip with sound plays under the selection."
573	        }
574	        return InspectorSection(
575	            id: "video.hide_silent", title: "Hide While Silent",
576	            summary: {

578	                let media = Set(gated().map { $0.video?.hideSilent?.media ?? 0 })
579	                guard allOn(), media.count == 1, let id = media.first,
580	                      let row = binding.snapshot.media(id)
581	                else { return "on" }
582	                return row.name
583	            },
584	            note: { problem.text },
585	            reset: { binding.apply(name, offOps()) },
586	            defaultExpanded: false,
587	            rows: [
588	                inspectorRow(
589	                    nil, [check], mixed: { anyOn() && !allOn() }, binding: binding,
590	                    writes: offOps(),
591	                    default: InspectorRowDefault(name: name, differs: anyOn, ops: offOps)),
592	                inspectorPopupRow(
593	                    "Speech from", binding, name: name, items: sourceList.map(\.name),
594	                    read: {

596	                    },
597	                    ops: { index in

3	/// The Clip tab's **Motion** section (spec §4.3, road map 5's E2) — what a
4	/// clip does on its way in, on its way out, and all the way through.
5	///
6	/// An `extension VideoPane` in a file of its own, `VideoPane+Transition.swift`'s
7	/// shape, because `VideoPane.swift` is over the size cap and may not grow.
8	///
9	/// **Every write is PER CLIP.** A `motion` patch replaces the whole object
10	/// (`MotionProps.dictionary` always writes three keys), so one `set_video`
11	/// over several ids would stamp the first clip's other two slots onto every
12	/// other clip. Each row therefore reads THAT clip's base motion, changes the
13	/// one slot or field, and emits that clip's own op — through
14	/// `ops(video:for:)`, whose `structural` puts motion on the base props even
15	/// inside an action. Reset alone is selection-wide, since every clip gets the
16	/// same value. Reads are the first clip's, the section rule.
17	extension VideoPane {
18	    // MARK: Motion
19	
20	    func motionSection() -> InspectorSection {
21	        let binding = self.binding
22	        let edges = EdgeMotion.allCases
23	        let durings = DuringMotion.allCases
24	        func motion() -> MotionProps { binding.videoProps.motion ?? MotionProps() }
25	        /// One op per clip over the selection's pixel clips; `step` answers
26	        /// the clip's next motion, or nil to skip the clip.
27	        func perClip(_ step: (ClipSnapshot, MotionProps) -> MotionProps?) -> [ReelOp] {
28	            var ops: [ReelOp] = []
29	            for clip in binding.videoClips {
30	                let current = clip.videoProps.motion ?? MotionProps()
31	                guard let next = step(clip, current) else { continue }
32	                ops.append(
33	                    contentsOf: binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(motion: .some(next)), for: clip))
34	            }
35	            return ops
36	        }
37	        func edgeKind(_ index: Int) -> EdgeMotion? {
38	            index == 0 ? nil : edges[min(max(index - 1, 0), edges.count - 1)]
39	        }
40	        /// A chosen kind keeps the slot's stored duration, else the core's
41	        /// own 0.5 s default (`MotionEdge()`).
42	        func edge(_ kind: EdgeMotion?, keeping stored: MotionEdge?) -> MotionEdge? {
43	            guard let kind = kind else { return nil }
44	            return MotionEdge(kind: kind, duration: stored?.duration ?? MotionEdge().duration)
45	        }
46	        func summary() -> String {
47	            let m = motion()
48	            var parts: [String] = []
49	            if let e = m.inEdge { parts.append("in " + e.displayName.lowercased()) }
50	            if let e = m.out { parts.append("out " + e.displayName.lowercased()) }
51	            if let d = m.during { parts.append(d.kind.displayName.lowercased()) }
52	            return parts.isEmpty ? "off" : parts.joined(separator: " · ")
53	        }
54	        func inactiveNote() -> String? {
55	            let selected = binding.videoClips.map { $0.videoProps.motion }
56	            let inactiveIn = selected.contains { $0?.inEdge.map { !$0.isActive } ?? false }
57	            let inactiveOut = selected.contains { $0?.out.map { !$0.isActive } ?? false }
58	            guard inactiveIn || inactiveOut else { return nil }
59	            let slots = [inactiveIn ? "In" : nil, inactiveOut ? "Out" : nil]
60	                .compactMap { $0 }.joined(separator: " and ")
61	            return "Selection includes inactive \(slots) motion (zero duration). "
62	                + "Increase Duration to reactivate; choose None to clear."
63	        }
64	
65	        let preview = commandButton(
66	            "Preview", #selector(EditorViewController.previewClipMotion(_:)),
67	            toolTip:
68	                "Play the clip in a loop: sets the in/out range to the clip and turns Loop on"
69	                + " — both stay until you clear them")
70	
71	        return InspectorSection(
72	            id: "video.motion", title: "Motion presets",
73	            summary: summary,
74	            reset: { binding.apply("Motion", video: VideoPatch(motion: .some(nil))) },
75	            defaultExpanded: false,
76	            rows: [
77	                InspectorNoteLabel(wraps: true, note: inactiveNote),
78	                inspectorPopupRow(
79	                    "In", binding, name: "Motion In", items: ["None"] + edges.map(\.displayName),
80	                    read: { motion().inEdge.map { (edges.firstIndex(of: $0.kind) ?? 0) + 1 } ?? 0 },
81	                    ops: { index in
82	                        perClip { _, m in
83	                            m.with { $0.inEdge = edge(edgeKind(index), keeping: m.inEdge) }
84	                        }
85	                    },
86	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.motion?.inEdge?.kind } }),
87	                // 0.1 s to 10 s: a few frames at the short end, and far longer
88	                // than any entrance is meant to take at the long one.
89	                inspectorValueRow(
90	                    "In Duration", binding, name: "Motion In Duration", unit: " s", decimals: 2,
91	                    min: 0.1, max: 10, quick: [0.25, 0.5, 1], slider: false,
92	                    read: { ReelTime.seconds(motion().inEdge?.duration ?? MotionEdge().duration) },
93	                    ops: { value in
94	                        perClip { _, m in
95	                            guard m.inEdge != nil else { return nil }
96	                            return m.with {
97	                                $0.inEdge?.duration = binding.frameTicks(seconds: value)
98	                            }
99	                        }
100	                    },
101	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.motion?.inEdge?.duration } },
102	                    enabled: { motion().inEdge != nil }),
103	                inspectorPopupRow(
104	                    "Out", binding, name: "Motion Out", items: ["None"] + edges.map(\.displayName),
105	                    read: { motion().out.map { (edges.firstIndex(of: $0.kind) ?? 0) + 1 } ?? 0 },
106	                    ops: { index in
107	                        perClip { _, m in
108	                            m.with { $0.out = edge(edgeKind(index), keeping: m.out) }
109	                        }
110	                    },
111	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.motion?.out?.kind } }),
112	                // The same range as In Duration, for the same reason.
113	                inspectorValueRow(
114	                    "Out Duration", binding, name: "Motion Out Duration", unit: " s", decimals: 2,
115	                    min: 0.1, max: 10, quick: [0.25, 0.5, 1], slider: false,
116	                    read: { ReelTime.seconds(motion().out?.duration ?? MotionEdge().duration) },
117	                    ops: { value in
118	                        perClip { _, m in
119	                            guard m.out != nil else { return nil }
120	                            return m.with { $0.out?.duration = binding.frameTicks(seconds: value) }
121	                        }
122	                    },
123	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.motion?.out?.duration } },
124	                    enabled: { motion().out != nil }),
125	                inspectorPopupRow(
126	                    "During", binding, name: "Motion During",
127	                    items: ["None"] + durings.map(\.displayName),
128	                    read: {
129	                        motion().during.map { (durings.firstIndex(of: $0.kind) ?? 0) + 1 } ?? 0
130	                    },
131	                    ops: { index in
132	                        perClip { _, m in
133	                            guard index > 0 else { return m.with { $0.during = nil } }
134	                            // A kind keeps the stored amount and period, else
135	                            // the core's own defaults (`MotionDuring()`).
136	                            var during = m.during ?? MotionDuring()
137	                            during.kind = durings[min(index - 1, durings.count - 1)]
138	                            return m.with { $0.during = during }
139	                        }
140	                    },
141	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.motion?.during?.kind } }),
142	                // Written as a percentage because the model's 0–1 reads as a
143	                // strength; `/ 100` at the write is the only conversion.
144	                inspectorValueRow(
145	                    "Amount", binding, name: "Motion Amount", unit: "%", decimals: 0,
146	                    min: 0, max: 100, quick: [25, 50, 75, 100], slider: false,
147	                    read: { (motion().during?.amount ?? MotionDuring().amount) * 100 },
148	                    ops: { value in
149	                        perClip { _, m in
150	                            guard m.during != nil else { return nil }
151	                            return m.with { $0.during?.amount = value / 100 }
152	                        }
153	                    },
154	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.motion?.during?.amount } },
155	                    enabled: { motion().during != nil }),
156	                // 0.1 s to 10 s: a cycle shorter than a few frames aliases, and
157	                // one longer than ten seconds no longer reads as a cycle.

161	                    min: 0.1, max: 10, quick: [0.25, 0.5, 1, 2], slider: false,
162	                    read: {

164	                    },

178	    }

182	extension VideoPane {
183	    // MARK: Obscure
184	
185	    /// The obscured regions (§4.3's phase-3c list, schema version 4): boxes
186	    /// on the layer whose contents are blurred or pixelated so a face, a
187	    /// password field or a notification cannot be read.
188	    ///
189	    /// It is the spotlight's inverse and it is spelled in the spotlight's
190	    /// frame — `x`/`y` are the region's CENTRE and `width`/`height` its size,
191	    /// both in SOURCE pixels from the centre of the cropped rect — so a
192	    /// region rides with its layer through scale, move and rotation, and the
193	    /// same four numbers typed into Spotlight put a box in the same place.
194	    /// That is also why the numeric rows are plain px fields rather than
195	    /// percentages, and why a centre outside the layer is allowed.
196	    ///
197	    /// **It is a LIST, so it takes `filtersSection`'s shape and its warning
198	    /// with it.** Nothing here is a general-purpose list editor and it must
199	    /// not become one: the cap is four, so every region is on screen at
200	    /// once; the rows are built against a FIXED INDEX (the count is in
201	    /// `structureSignature`, so add and remove rebuild the pane while
202	    /// dialling a value merely refreshes it); an index the model no longer
203	    /// holds yields the list unchanged, which the core answers as the
204	    /// identity it is; and every write sends the WHOLE array through an
205	    /// ordinary `set_video` patch, which is what keeps add and remove out of
206	    /// the op table (`actions::merge` replaces arrays wholesale).
207	    ///
208	    /// **Adding and removing a region change the CLIP**, not the action under
209	    /// the playhead — including "Place on Canvas", which is an append like
210	    /// any other. A list of a different length in an action's end patch
211	    /// cannot interpolate, so an appended region would be invisible for the
212	    /// whole span and gone at the next write; dialling an existing region's
213	    /// amount or box still belongs to the action, which is what §3c's
214	    /// interpolation rule is for. `InspectorBinding.structural(video:for:)`
215	    /// decides it, for this list and the filter stack alike, and argues it in
216	    /// full.
217	    ///
218	    /// Order does NOT matter here, unlike the filter stack: where two
219	    /// regions overlap the shader takes the STRONGER of them per fragment,
220	    /// so there is no position popup to move a region up or down and the
221	    /// label column carries the region's number instead.
222	    ///
223	    /// **One "Place on Canvas", not one per row.** It appends, and it is
224	    /// disabled at the cap. `InspectorViewController.onCommand` is
225	    /// `(Selector) -> Void` and carries no index (`inspectorCommand` sends a
226	    /// nil sender), so a per-row button would need an index-carrying seam of
227	    /// its own — the first of its kind, added for one button, against the
228	    /// warning above. A region placed on the canvas is edited in its row like
229	    /// any other.
230	    func obscureSection() -> InspectorSection {
231	        let binding = self.binding
232	        let shapes = SpotShape.allCases
233	        let kinds = ObscureKind.allCases
234	        func list() -> [ObscureProps] { binding.videoProps.obscure }
235	        func at(_ index: Int) -> ObscureProps? {
236	            let regions = list()
237	            return regions.indices.contains(index) ? regions[index] : nil
238	        }
239	        func ops(_ next: [ObscureProps]) -> [ReelOp] {
240	            binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(obscure: next))
241	        }
242	        /// The read/write split the filter stack takes, for the same reason
243	        /// and out of the same reader: inside an action a write REPLACES the
244	        /// end patch's array whole, so building it from the interpolated
245	        /// regions would pin every one the user did not touch — and with
246	        /// eight fields a region, seven of them ride along on every edit.
247	        func writeList() -> [ObscureProps] {
248	            binding.editedList(action: { $0.obscure }, base: { $0.obscure })
249	        }
250	        func writeAt(_ index: Int) -> ObscureProps? {
251	            let regions = writeList()
252	            return regions.indices.contains(index) ? regions[index] : nil
253	        }
254	        func replacing(_ index: Int, _ next: ObscureProps) -> [ObscureProps] {
255	            var regions = writeList()
256	            guard regions.indices.contains(index) else { return regions }
257	            regions[index] = next
258	            return regions
259	        }
260	        /// One region with `change` applied, the other fields as they stand —
261	        /// `spotlightSection`'s `edited { … }` over a list. Eight fields is
262	        /// enough that spelling all of them out at every row would bury the
263	        /// one that changes. No change is the region rewritten as it is.
264	        func edited(
265	            _ index: Int, _ change: (inout ObscureProps) -> Void = { _ in }
266	        ) -> [ReelOp] {
267	            // `writeAt`, not `at`: the seven fields that ride along are the
268	            // ones the edit is replacing, never the ones the playhead shows.
269	            guard var o = writeAt(index) else { return [] }
270	            change(&o)
271	            return ops(replacing(index, o))
272	        }
273	        /// The mixed badge for one region's field: a selection where some
274	        /// clip has no region at that index disagrees, which the `nil` says.
275	        func mixedAt<T: Equatable>(_ index: Int, _ read: @escaping (ObscureProps) -> T) -> Bool {
276	            binding.mixedVideo { props in
277	                props.obscure.indices.contains(index) ? read(props.obscure[index]) : nil
278	            }
279	        }
280	        /// The paired numeric boxes. Centre and size get two fields on one
281	        /// row rather than the four separate value rows the spotlight gives
282	        /// them: four regions × eight rows would be a section nobody can see
283	        /// the end of, and neither pair wants a slider anyway (§4.3 gives
284	        /// the spotlight's own centre and size `slider: false`).
285	        func field(
286	            _ index: Int, name: String, min lower: Double, max upper: Double,
287	            quick: [Double] = [], read: @escaping (ObscureProps) -> Double,
288	            write: @escaping (Int, Double) -> [ReelOp]
289	        ) -> OptionFieldControl {
290	            OptionFieldControl(
291	                width: InspectorMetrics.fieldWidth, unit: " px", decimals: 0, min: lower,
292	                max: upper, quick: quick,
293	                read: { at(index).map(read) ?? 0 },
294	                write: { value in binding.apply(name, write(index, value)) },
295	                enabled: { true },
296	                onEdit: { binding.edited() })
297	        }
298	
299	        let count = list().count
300	        var rows: [NSView] = []
301	        for index in 0..<count {
302	            let kind = OptionPopupControl(
303	                width: 96, items: kinds.map { $0.displayName },
304	                read: { kinds.firstIndex(of: at(index)?.kind ?? .pixelate) ?? 0 },
305	                write: { choice in
306	                    guard kinds.indices.contains(choice) else { return }
307	                    binding.apply("Obscure Kind", edited(index) { $0.kind = kinds[choice] })
308	                },
309	                enabled: { true },
310	                onEdit: { binding.edited() })
311	            kind.toolTip = "Pixelate hides; blur softens"
312	            let remove = OptionButtonControl(
313	                title: "Remove",
314	                action: {
315	                    var next = list()
316	                    guard next.indices.contains(index) else {
317	                        NSSound.beep()
318	                        return
319	                    }
320	                    next.remove(at: index)
321	                    binding.apply("Remove Region", ops(next))
322	                },
323	                enabled: { true }, onEdit: {})
324	            remove.toolTip =
325	                "Take this region off the clip — the clip itself, not the action "
326	                + "under the playhead"
327	            rows.append(
328	                inspectorRow(
329	                    "Region \(index + 1)", [kind, remove],
330	                    mixed: { mixedAt(index) { $0.kind } },
331	                    binding: binding, writes: edited(index)))
332	            rows.append(
333	                inspectorPopupRow(
334	                    "Shape", binding, name: "Obscure Shape",
335	                    items: shapes.map { $0.displayName },
336	                    read: { shapes.firstIndex(of: at(index)?.shape ?? .rect) ?? 0 },
337	                    ops: { choice in
338	                        guard shapes.indices.contains(choice) else { return [] }
339	                        return edited(index) { $0.shape = shapes[choice] }
340	                    },
341	                    mixed: { mixedAt(index) { $0.shape } }))
342	            rows.append(
343	                inspectorValueRow(
344	                    "Amount", binding, name: "Obscure Amount", unit: "%", decimals: 0, min: 0,
345	                    max: 100, quick: [0, 25, 50, 75, 100],
346	                    read: { (at(index)?.amount ?? 0) * 100 },
347	                    ops: { v in edited(index) { $0.amount = v / 100 } },
348	                    mixed: { mixedAt(index) { $0.amount } }))
349	            rows.append(
350	                inspectorValueRow(
351	                    "Feather", binding, name: "Obscure Feather", unit: " px", decimals: 0,
352	                    min: 0, max: 200, quick: [0, 10, 20, 40, 80],
353	                    read: { at(index)?.feather ?? 0 },
354	                    ops: { v in edited(index) { $0.feather = v } },
355	                    mixed: { mixedAt(index) { $0.feather } }))
356	            rows.append(
357	                inspectorRow(
358	                    "Center",
359	                    [
360	                        field(
361	                            index, name: "Obscure Center", min: -20000, max: 20000,
362	                            read: { $0.x }, write: { i, value in edited(i) { $0.x = value } }),
363	                        field(
364	                            index, name: "Obscure Center", min: -20000, max: 20000,
365	                            read: { $0.y }, write: { i, value in edited(i) { $0.y = value } }),
366	                    ],
367	                    mixed: { mixedAt(index) { $0.x } || mixedAt(index) { $0.y } },
368	                    binding: binding, writes: edited(index)))
369	            // The core takes width and height as strictly greater than zero
370	            // (`above`, not `at_least`), exactly as it does the spotlight's:
371	            // a region with no area hides nothing and cannot be grabbed back,
372	            // so the field's floor is one pixel rather than nought.
373	            rows.append(
374	                inspectorRow(
375	                    "Size",
376	                    [
377	                        field(
378	                            index, name: "Obscure Size", min: 1, max: 20000,
379	                            quick: [120, 240, 480, 960], read: { $0.width },
380	                            write: { i, value in edited(i) { $0.width = value } }),
381	                        field(
382	                            index, name: "Obscure Size", min: 1, max: 20000,
383	                            quick: [68, 135, 270, 540], read: { $0.height },
384	                            write: { i, value in edited(i) { $0.height = value } }),
385	                    ],
386	                    mixed: { mixedAt(index) { $0.width } || mixedAt(index) { $0.height } },
387	                    binding: binding, writes: edited(index)))
388	        }
389	        if count == 0 {
390	            rows.append(inspectorRow(nil, [InspectorRowLabel("No obscured regions.")]))
391	        }
392	        let add = OptionButtonControl(
393	            title: "Add Region",
394	            action: {
395	                var next = list()
396	                guard next.count < ObscureProps.max else {
397	                    NSSound.beep()
398	                    return
399	                }
400	                next.append(ObscureProps())
401	                binding.apply("Add Region", ops(next))
402	            },
403	            enabled: { list().count < ObscureProps.max }, onEdit: {})
404	        add.toolTip =
405	            "Add a 480 × 270 pixelated box at the centre of the layer — on the clip "
406	            + "itself, not on the action under the playhead"
407	        let place = commandButton(
408	            "Place on Canvas", #selector(EditorViewController.placeObscureRegion(_:)),
409	            toolTip:
410	                "Drag a rectangle on the canvas (Esc cancels) — it is appended to the clip "

413	        rows.append(

415

497	    /// One range's two rows: the checkbox and the strip, then the fields.
498	    private func qualifierRows(
499	        _ range: QualifierRange, read: @escaping () -> ColorQualifier,
500	        ops: @escaping (ColorQualifierPatch) -> [ReelOp]
501	    ) -> [NSView] {
502	        let binding = self.binding
503	        let name = range.title
504	        func on() -> Bool { read().isOn(range) }
505	        let check = OptionCheckboxControl(
506	            label: name, read: on,
507	            write: { [weak binding] value in
508	                binding?.apply(name, ops(.toggle(range, value)))
509	            },
510	            enabled: { true },
511	            onEdit: { [weak binding] in binding?.edited() })
512	        check.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
513	        check.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: InspectorMetrics.labelWidth).isActive = true
514	        let strip = RangeStripControl(
515	            kind: range, read: read,
516	            begin: { [weak binding] in binding?.liveBegin() },
517	            update: { [weak binding] patch in binding?.liveUpdate(ops(patch)) },
518	            end: { [weak binding] in binding?.liveEnd(name) })
519	        let mixed: () -> Bool
520	        switch range {
521	        case .hue: mixed = { binding.mixedVideo { $0.qualifier.hue } }
522	        case .saturation: mixed = { binding.mixedVideo { $0.qualifier.saturation } }

534	    /// The range's three captioned fields across one row.
535	    private func qualifierFields(
536	        _ range: QualifierRange, read: @escaping () -> ColorQualifier,
537	        ops: @escaping (ColorQualifierPatch) -> [ReelOp]
538	    ) -> NSView {
539	        let binding = self.binding
540	        let name = range.title
541	        func on() -> Bool { read().isOn(range) }
542	        typealias Field = (caption: String, max: Double, get: (ColorQualifier) -> Double,
543	                           put: (ColorQualifier, Double) -> ColorQualifierPatch)
544	        let fields: [Field]
545	        if range == .hue {
546	            func hue(_ q: ColorQualifier) -> QualifierHue { q.hue ?? .initial }
547	            fields = [
548	                ("Centre", 360, { hue($0).center },
549	                 { q, v in var h = hue(q); h.center = v; return ColorQualifierPatch(hue: .set(h)) }),
550	                ("Width", 360, { hue($0).width },
551	                 { q, v in var h = hue(q); h.width = v; return ColorQualifierPatch(hue: .set(h)) }),
552	                ("Soft", 180, { hue($0).softness },
553	                 { q, v in var h = hue(q); h.softness = v; return ColorQualifierPatch(hue: .set(h)) }),
554	            ]
555	        } else {
556	            func levels(_ q: ColorQualifier) -> QualifierLevels { q.levels(range) ?? .initial }
557	            fields = [
558	                ("Low", 1, { levels($0).low },
559	                 { q, v in
560	                     var l = levels(q)
561	                     l.low = min(v, l.high)
562	                     return .levels(range, .set(l))
563	                 }),
564	                ("High", 1, { levels($0).high },
565	                 { q, v in
566	                     var l = levels(q)
567	                     l.high = max(v, l.low)
568	                     return .levels(range, .set(l))
569	                 }),
570	                ("Soft", 1, { levels($0).softness },
571	                 { q, v in var l = levels(q); l.softness = v; return .levels(range, .set(l)) }),
572	            ]
573	        }
574	        var controls: [NSView] = []
575	        for field in fields {
576	            let caption = InspectorRowLabel(field.caption)
577	            caption.font = DS.sans(10)
578	            caption.setContentCompressionResistancePriority(.required, for: .horizontal)
579	            controls.append(caption)
580	            controls.append(
581	                OptionFieldControl(
582	                    width: 41, unit: range == .hue ? "°" : "", decimals: range == .hue ? 0 : 2,
583	                    min: 0, max: field.max,
584	                    read: { field.get(read()) },
585	                    write: { [weak binding] value in
586	                        binding?.apply(name, ops(field.put(read(), value)))
587	                    },
588	                    enabled: on,
589	                    onEdit: { [weak binding] in binding?.edited() }))
590	        }
591	        return inspectorRow(nil, controls, binding: binding, writes: ops(.reset))
592	    }

730	/// The Clip tab's **Transition** section (spec §4.3) — the one group that is
731	/// not about the layer's own pixels but about how it MEETS the clip before
732	/// it. `ClipPane` shows it only for a single clip with an overlap
733	/// (`ClipPane.makeSections()`), which is the only state in which an overlap
734	/// has a transition to describe.
735	///
736	/// An `extension VideoPane` in a file of its own because `VideoPane.swift`
737	/// stood at 1465 lines against the ~400-line rule for new files and the
738	/// section is about to grow the Curve popup and the Crossfade Audio check
739	/// row road map 5's E1 adds. The move cost no visibility: `binding` is
740	/// internal and the row builders are free functions.
741	extension VideoPane {
742	    // MARK: Transition
743	
744	    /// The section's five rows: which transition, how it is eased, whether
745	    /// it crossfades the sound and in which shape (format 29, spec §11
746	    /// AU-115; enabled while Crossfade Audio is on), and how long the
747	    /// overlap is.
748	    ///
749	    /// **The Curve and Crossfade Audio rows READ the snapshot's lenient
750	    /// defaults** — `linear` and `false` — which is what a clip with no
751	    /// stored transition draws, and what a version-6 file's transition
752	    /// means. They deliberately do not show what the core would MINT: the
753	    /// section has to say what is there.
754	    ///
755	    /// **And when `transitionIn` is nil, each of the three sends every key.**
756	    /// The Kind popup's index 0 is None, so a clip under an overlap is one
757	    /// click away from having no stored transition at all while still being
758	    /// drawn as a cross dissolve; a one-key `set_transition_style` on that
759	    /// clip would mint `ease_in_out`/`true` underneath and the untouched
760	    /// row would silently change its value. Sending both makes the minted
761	    /// transition exactly what the section was showing, with only the
762	    /// touched value moved. With a transition stored, each row sends its one
763	    /// key and the core keeps the other. `TextPane`'s animation section is
764	    /// the precedent, applied to two scalars rather than to one object.
765	    func transitionSection(_ clip: UInt32) -> InspectorSection {
766	        let binding = self.binding
767	        let kinds = TransitionKind.allCases
768	        let items = ["None"] + kinds.map { $0.displayName }
769	        let curves = Curve.allCases
770	        /// The overlap read fresh: changing the duration MOVES the clip
771	        /// (§6 `set_transition_duration`), so the captured start would be
772	        /// wrong one edit later.
773	        func overlapSeconds() -> Double {
774	            guard let current = binding.snapshot.clip(clip) else { return 0 }
775	            let earlier = binding.snapshot.clips(onTrack: current.track)
776	                .filter { $0.start < current.start }
777	            guard let previous = earlier.last else { return 0 }
778	            return ReelTime.seconds(max(previous.end - current.start, 0))
779	        }
780	        func stored() -> TransitionSnapshot? { binding.snapshot.clip(clip)?.transitionIn }
781	        func curve() -> Curve { stored()?.curve ?? .linear }
782	        func crossfades() -> Bool { stored()?.audio ?? false }
783	        let shapes = FadeShape.allCases
784	        func shape() -> FadeShape { stored()?.audioShape ?? .plus3Db }
785	        /// The style write, carrying the other rows' DISPLAYED values too
786	        /// whenever there is nothing stored to keep them (see the doc above).
787	        func styleOps(curve next: Curve?, audio: Bool?, shape nextShape: FadeShape? = nil)
788	            -> [ReelOp]
789	        {
790	            if stored() == nil {
791	                return [
792	                    .setTransitionStyle(
793	                        clip: clip, curve: next ?? curve(), audio: audio ?? crossfades(),
794	                        audioShape: nextShape ?? shape())
795	                ]
796	            }
797	            return [
798	                .setTransitionStyle(clip: clip, curve: next, audio: audio, audioShape: nextShape)
799	            ]
800	        }
801	        return InspectorSection(
802	            id: "video.transition", title: "Transition",
803	            summary: {
804	                guard let transition = stored() else { return "none" }
805	                return transition.kind.displayName.lowercased()
806	                    + " · " + transition.curve.displayName.lowercased()
807	                    + String(format: " · %.2f s", overlapSeconds())
808	            },
809	            defaultExpanded: false,
810	            rows: [
811	                inspectorPopupRow(
812	                    "Kind", binding, name: "Set Transition", items: items,
813	                    read: {
814	                        guard let kind = binding.snapshot.clip(clip)?.transitionIn?.kind else {
815	                            return 0
816	                        }
817	                        return (kinds.firstIndex(of: kind) ?? 0) + 1
818	                    },
819	                    ops: { index in
820	                        let kind = index == 0 ? nil : kinds[min(max(index - 1, 0), kinds.count - 1)]
821	                        return [.setTransition(clip: clip, kind: kind)]
822	                    }, resets: false),
823	                inspectorPopupRow(
824	                    "Curve", binding, name: "Transition Curve",
825	                    items: curves.map { $0.displayName },
826	                    read: { curves.firstIndex(of: curve()) ?? 0 },
827	                    ops: { index in
828	                        styleOps(
829	                            curve: curves[min(max(index, 0), curves.count - 1)], audio: nil)
830	                    }, resets: false),
831	                inspectorCheckRow(
832	                    "Crossfade Audio", binding, name: "Transition Audio",
833	                    read: crossfades,
834	                    ops: { value in styleOps(curve: nil, audio: value) }, resets: false),
835	                inspectorPopupRow(
836	                    "Crossfade Shape", binding, name: "Crossfade Shape",
837	                    items: shapes.map { $0.title },
838	                    read: { shapes.firstIndex(of: shape()) ?? 0 },
839	                    ops: { index in
840	                        styleOps(
841	                            curve: nil, audio: nil,
842	                            shape: shapes[min(max(index, 0), shapes.count - 1)])
843	                    }, enabled: crossfades, resets: false),
844	                inspectorValueRow(
845	                    "Duration", binding, name: "Transition Duration", unit: " s", decimals: 2,
846	                    min: 0.02, max: 10, quick: [0.25, 0.5, 1, 2], slider: false,
847	                    read: overlapSeconds,
848	                    ops: { value in
849	                        [
850	                            .setTransitionDuration(
851	                                clip: clip,
852	                                duration: binding.frameTicks(seconds: value))
853	                        ]
854	                    }, resets: false),
855	            ])
856	    }

1063	    private func stripBegan(_ kind: ColorWheelKind, binding: InspectorBinding?) {
1064	        stripStarts[kind] = binding?.document?.project

1069	    /// A strip's release: the live trio's end, then the handle it left,
1070	    /// kept only when the gesture registered a step (the handle moved).
1071	    private func stripEnded(_ kind: ColorWheelKind, name: String, binding: InspectorBinding?) {
1072	        binding?.liveEnd(name)
1073	        if let after = binding?.document?.project, after !== stripStarts[kind] {
1074	            stripSteps[kind] = (after, ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime)
1075	        }
1076	        stripStarts[kind] = nil
1077	    }

1079	    /// A strip's double-click: the reset amends the step its first click
1080	    /// left when that release is within the double-click interval — so an
1081	    /// earlier gesture's step is never reused — and is its own step
1082	    /// otherwise.
1083	    private func stripReset(
1084	        _ kind: ColorWheelKind, name: String, binding: InspectorBinding?, ops: [ReelOp]
1085	    ) {
1086	        let last = stripSteps.removeValue(forKey: kind)
1087	        if let last,
1088	            ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime - last.at <= NSEvent.doubleClickInterval
1089	        {
1090	            binding?.amend(name, ops, step: last.step)
1091	        } else {
1092	            binding?.apply(name, ops)
1093	        }
1094	    }

1141	    /// has them removed from its base (`null`); a clip inside one has each
1142	    /// channel whose edited curve is not its domain's identity written to the

1161	            for channel in channels { removed = removed.setting(channel, .some(nil)) }

3	/// The Clip tab's PIXEL sections (spec §4.3): Transform, Crop, Corner Radius,
4	/// Colour, Chroma Key, Filters, Reflection, Spotlight, Obscure, Speed and —
5	/// when the clip overlaps its predecessor — Transition.
6	///
7	/// **This pane is never shown.** Since the six tabs became three it is a
8	/// factory: `ClipPane` holds one instance and calls the section methods below
9	/// in the order the design asks for, mixing them with the audio, text and
10	/// shape panes' sections according to what is selected. Everything here still
11	/// reads and writes through the shared `InspectorBinding`, so the sections do
12	/// not care which pane built them. `structureSignature` is still this pane's
13	/// job — `ClipPane` composes it with the other three.
14	///
15	/// Text and shape clips get the groups that measure the layer against itself
16	/// — Transform, Opacity, Shadow, Filters, Reflection and Spotlight — but not
17	/// the ones that need a decoded frame behind them, which is why Crop, Corner
18	/// Radius, Colour and Chroma Key are gated on `allSourcePixels` and Speed on
19	/// `allMedia` (only a `media` source accepts `set_speed`, §6). Filters,
20	/// Reflection and Spotlight follow Shadow's precedent rather than Chroma's:
21	/// their lengths are source pixels and their strengths are fractions of the
22	/// layer's own rectangle, both of which a text or shape layer has (the
23	/// renderer measures it). A section that does not apply is absent rather than
24	/// disabled: the pane is rebuilt when the selection's kinds change, so there
25	/// is nothing stale to grey out.
26	final class VideoPane: InspectorPaneView {
27	    // MARK: - Applicability
28	
29	    /// Clips whose rectangle comes from decoded pixels — the ones with a crop,
30	    /// a colour treatment and a corner radius.
31	    var allSourcePixels: Bool {
32	        let clips = binding.clips
33	        return !clips.isEmpty
34	            && clips.allSatisfy { InspectorTab.hasSourcePixels($0, in: binding.snapshot) }
35	    }
36	
37	    /// Clips `set_speed` accepts (§6: a non-media source is an error).
38	    var allMedia: Bool {
39	        let clips = binding.clips
40	        return !clips.isEmpty && clips.allSatisfy { $0.source.hasSourceBound }
41	    }

43	    /// The overlap with the previous clip on the same track, when there is
44	    /// one. That overlap IS the transition's duration (§5.2).
45	    func overlap(before clip: ClipSnapshot) -> Ticks? {
46	        let earlier = binding.snapshot.clips(onTrack: clip.track).filter { $0.start < clip.start }
47	        guard let previous = earlier.last else { return nil }
48	        let overlap = previous.end - clip.start
49	        return overlap > 0 ? overlap : nil
50	    }

52	    override var structureSignature: String {
53	        var parts = [super.structureSignature]
54	        parts.append(allSourcePixels ? "px" : "-")
55	        parts.append(allMedia ? "media" : "-")
56	        // The filter stack is one of the two sections whose ROW COUNT comes
57	        // from the model, so its length belongs here: adding or removing a
58	        // filter has to rebuild the pane, while re-ordering or re-dialling
59	        // one only refreshes it (the rows read by index, so the values
60	        // simply move).
61	        parts.append("f\(binding.videoProps.filters.count)")
62	        // The obscure list is the second one, and for the same reason: Add,
63	        // Remove and "Place on Canvas" all change how many rows the section
64	        // has, while dialling a region's amount only changes what they read.
65	        parts.append("o\(binding.videoProps.obscure.count)")
66	        if binding.isSingle, let clip = binding.primary {
67	            parts.append(clip.actions.map { String($0.id) }.joined(separator: "."))
68	            parts.append(overlap(before: clip) != nil ? "transition" : "-")
69	        }
70	        return parts.joined(separator: "|")
71	    }

230	
231	    /// The filter stack (§4.3's M3 list), at most `FilterProps.max` deep.
232	    ///
233	    /// **Order is the whole point.** The compositor applies `video.filters`
234	    /// in the order they are listed, so blur-then-sepia and sepia-then-blur
235	    /// are different pictures, and a control set that cannot say which comes
236	    /// first would be lying about what the layer does. That is why each
237	    /// filter's row leads with a POSITION popup rather than an ordinal label:
238	    /// the number both shows where the filter sits and is the thing that
239	    /// moves it. It occupies the label column the rest of the inspector
240	    /// already reserves, where a Move Up / Move Down pair costs two controls
241	    /// beyond it and up-only costs one plus a dead first row; and with four
242	    /// slots it reaches any order in one gesture rather than three.
243	    ///
244	    /// Nothing here is a general-purpose list editor, and it must not become
245	    /// one: the cap is four, so the whole stack is on screen at once, the
246	    /// rows are built against a fixed index (the count is in
247	    /// `structureSignature`, so add and remove rebuild the pane while a
248	    /// re-order merely refreshes it), and every write sends the WHOLE array.
249	    /// That last point is what keeps add, remove and re-order ordinary
250	    /// `set_video` patches instead of three new ops — `actions::merge`
251	    /// replaces arrays wholesale rather than merging them element by element.
252	    ///
253	    /// Adding and removing a filter change the CLIP, not the action under the
254	    /// playhead, even when the section's note says an edit here lands on an
255	    /// action's end state: a list of a different length in an end patch
256	    /// cannot interpolate, so it would be invisible for the whole span and
257	    /// destroyed by the next write. `InspectorBinding.structural(video:for:)`
258	    /// is where that is decided, for this list and the obscure one alike, and
259	    /// it argues the whole rule.
260	    ///
261	    /// **A row READS the evaluated stack and WRITES the one it is replacing**,
262	    /// which are the same array everywhere except inside an action —
263	    /// `writeList()` below, and `InspectorBinding.editedList`, which argues it.
264	    /// One residual is left deliberately: Add and Remove still build from the
265	    /// evaluated stack, because `structural` routes them to the BASE props and
266	    /// the entries they carry across are therefore the values at the playhead
267	    /// rather than the clip's own. It is the same family of defect one step
268	    /// out, it is older than the write list, and fixing it means deciding
269	    /// which of two arrays an add is really an edit of — a question the length
270	    /// rule above does not answer.
271	    func filtersSection() -> InspectorSection {
272	        let binding = self.binding
273	        let kinds = FilterKind.allCases
274	        func list() -> [FilterProps] { binding.videoProps.filters }
275	        func at(_ index: Int) -> FilterProps? {
276	            let filters = list()
277	            return filters.indices.contains(index) ? filters[index] : nil
278	        }
279	        func ops(_ next: [FilterProps]) -> [ReelOp] {
280	            binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(filters: next))
281	        }
282	        /// The stack an EDIT is built on, which inside an action is not the
283	        /// one the rows are showing: the action's own end `filters` when its
284	        /// end patch carries them, the clip's base stack otherwise
285	        /// (`InspectorBinding.editedList`, which argues it). `list()` above
286	        /// stays the read — every row goes on showing the picture at the
287	        /// playhead — and this is the write. Without the pair, dialling one
288	        /// filter re-sent every OTHER filter at its interpolated value and
289	        /// flattened its ramp.
290	        func writeList() -> [FilterProps] {
291	            binding.editedList(action: { $0.filters }, base: { $0.filters })
292	        }
293	        func writeAt(_ index: Int) -> FilterProps? {
294	            let filters = writeList()
295	            return filters.indices.contains(index) ? filters[index] : nil
296	        }
297	        /// One slot changed, the rest of the stack as it stands. An index the
298	        /// model no longer holds yields the list unchanged, which the core
299	        /// answers as the identity it is — the same beep a refusal gets, no
300	        /// undo step either way. The row is a frame behind its rebuild there,
301	        /// and a guess about which filter was meant would be worse.
302	        func replacing(_ index: Int, _ next: FilterProps) -> [FilterProps] {
303	            var filters = writeList()
304	            guard filters.indices.contains(index) else { return filters }
305	            filters[index] = next
306	            return filters
307	        }
308	
309	        let count = list().count
310	        func row(_ index: Int) -> NSView {
311	            let order = OptionPopupControl(
312	                width: InspectorMetrics.labelWidth,
313	                items: (1...Swift.max(count, 1)).map { String($0) },
314	                read: { index },
315	                write: { position in
316	                    // The write list, not the read one: a re-order keeps the
317	                    // LENGTH, so it lands on the action's end patch like any
318	                    // other dial, and building it from the evaluated stack
319	                    // would pin every filter's amount on its way past.
320	                    var next = writeList()
321	                    guard next.indices.contains(index), next.indices.contains(position),
322	                          position != index
323	                    else { return }
324	                    next.insert(next.remove(at: index), at: position)
325	                    binding.apply("Reorder Filters", ops(next))
326	                },
327	                enabled: { true },
328	                onEdit: { binding.edited() })
329	            order.toolTip = "Where this filter sits in the stack; they are applied in order"
330	            let kind = OptionPopupControl(
331	                width: 92, items: kinds.map { $0.displayName },
332	                read: { kinds.firstIndex(of: at(index)?.kind ?? .blur) ?? 0 },
333	                write: { choice in
334	                    // `writeAt`, so the amount carried alongside the new kind
335	                    // is the one the edit is replacing rather than the one
336	                    // under the playhead.
337	                    guard let filter = writeAt(index), kinds.indices.contains(choice)
338	                    else { return }
339	                    binding.apply(
340	                        "Filter Kind",
341	                        ops(
342	                            replacing(
343	                                index, FilterProps(kind: kinds[choice], amount: filter.amount))))
344	                },
345	                enabled: { true },
346	                onEdit: { binding.edited() })
347	            let remove = OptionButtonControl(
348	                title: "Remove",
349	                action: {
350	                    var next = list()
351	                    guard next.indices.contains(index) else {
352	                        NSSound.beep()
353	                        return
354	                    }
355	                    next.remove(at: index)
356	                    binding.apply("Remove Filter", ops(next))
357	                },
358	                enabled: { true }, onEdit: {})
359	            remove.toolTip =
360	                "Take this filter off the clip — the stack itself, not the action "
361	                + "under the playhead"
362	            return inspectorRow(
363	                nil, [order, kind, remove],
364	                mixed: {
365	                    binding.mixedVideo { props in
366	                        props.filters.indices.contains(index) ? props.filters[index].kind : nil
367	                    }
368	                }, binding: binding, writes: ops(writeList()))
369	        }
370	
371	        var rows: [NSView] = []
372	        for index in 0..<count {
373	            rows.append(row(index))
374	            rows.append(
375	                inspectorValueRow(
376	                    "Amount", binding, name: "Filter Amount", unit: "%", decimals: 0, min: 0,
377	                    max: 100, quick: [0, 25, 50, 75, 100],
378	                    read: { (at(index)?.amount ?? 0) * 100 },
379	                    ops: { value in
380	                        guard let filter = writeAt(index) else { return [] }
381	                        return ops(
382	                            replacing(index, FilterProps(kind: filter.kind, amount: value / 100)))
383	                    },
384	                    mixed: {
385	                        binding.mixedVideo { props in
386	                            props.filters.indices.contains(index)
387	                                ? props.filters[index].amount : nil
388	                        }
389	                    }))
390	        }
391	        if count == 0 {
392	            rows.append(inspectorRow(nil, [InspectorRowLabel("No filters on this clip.")]))
393	        }
394	        let add = OptionButtonControl(
395	            title: "Add Filter",
396	            action: {
397	                var next = list()
398	                guard next.count < FilterProps.max else {
399	                    NSSound.beep()
400	                    return
401	                }
402	                next.append(FilterProps())
403	                binding.apply("Add Filter", ops(next))
404	            },
405	            enabled: { list().count < FilterProps.max }, onEdit: {})
406	        add.toolTip =
407	            "Append a half-strength blur to the end of the stack — on the clip itself, "
408	            + "not on the action under the playhead"
409	        rows.append(
410	            inspectorButtonRow([add, InspectorRowLabel("\(FilterProps.max) at most")]))
411	
412	        return InspectorSection(
413	            id: "video.filters", title: "Filters",
414	            summary: {
415	                let stack = list()
416	                guard !stack.isEmpty else { return "none" }
417	                return stack.count == 1
418	                    ? stack[0].kind.displayName.lowercased() : "\(stack.count) filters"
419	            },
420	            reset: { binding.apply("Filters", video: VideoPatch(filters: [])) },
421	            differs: { !list().isEmpty },
422	            defaultExpanded: false,
423	            rows: rows)
424	    }

513	    /// It lives HERE and not in the Shape pane, where spec §4.3 first listed
514	    /// it, because the zoom half can only be drawn by the layer that owns the
515	    /// pixels: a separate darkening shape could dim the frame but could never
516	    /// magnify it. The centre and the box are SOURCE pixels measured from the
517	    /// centre of the cropped rect — the same frame Crop and Corner Radius use
518	    /// — so they are plain px fields rather than percentages, and the centre

631	        let binding = self.binding
632	        let modes = BlendMode.allCases
633	        // Built by hand rather than with `inspectorPopupRow` for one reason:
634	        // the row builder has nowhere to hang a tooltip, and this is the
635	        // control in the app that most needs one — the note below fires only

639	            width: InspectorMetrics.popupWidth, items: modes.map { $0.displayName },

642	                guard modes.indices.contains(index) else { return }
643	                binding.apply("Blend Mode", video: VideoPatch(blend: modes[index]))
644	            },
645	            // Disabled on a nest clip, where the core refuses every mode but
646	            // `normal` (`edit_props.rs`'s `check_blend`) and an enabled popup
647	            // could only raise an error sheet for a row the panel itself
648	            // offered. `shape.radius`'s `enabled: { kind == .rectangle }` and
649	            // this phase's own gradient rows are the convention: a control
650	            // that cannot land is greyed, never allowed to fail.
651	            enabled: { VideoPane.blendApplies(to: binding.videoClips) },
652	            onEdit: { binding.edited() })
653	        blend.toolTip =
654	            "How this layer combines with what is already on the canvas. A blend needs "
655	            + "something UNDER it: over the empty canvas multiply, darken and overlay read "
656	            + "black, and screen, add, lighten and difference change nothing at all — "
657	            + "Clip ▸ Add Background puts a plate on the back track to blend against. A "
658	            + "cross dissolve draws as normal for the length of the overlap."
659	        return InspectorSection(
660	            id: "video.transform", title: "Transform",
661	            summary: {
662	                let props = binding.videoProps
663	                let scale = String(format: "%.0f%%", props.scale * 100)
664	                guard abs(props.rotation) >= 0.05 else { return scale }
665	                return scale + String(format: " · %.0f°", props.rotation)
666	            },
667	            // The nest note first, which says why a row is GREY — a disabled
668	            // control the reader cannot explain outranks a warning about one
669	            // that works — and the blend note last, since it only ever
670	            // appears when the mode is one that cannot be seen at all.
671	            note: { [weak self] in
672	                self?.nestBlendNote() ?? self?.blendNote()
673	            },
674	            reset: {

794	    /// The Transform section's note when a blend mode has nothing to blend
795	    /// with — the one trap this feature has, and the reason a person's first
796	    /// try at it looks broken.
797	    ///
798	    /// Every mode but `normal` is a function of two colours, and the canvas
799	    /// starts as its background (black, unless the Document tab says
800	    /// otherwise). So a layer with nothing under it and a non-normal mode is
801	    /// either black — `multiply`, `darken` and `overlay` all collapse when the
802	    /// destination is 0 — or exactly what it was, since `screen`, `add`,
803	    /// `lighten` and `difference` are all the identity against 0. Neither
804	    /// looks like a mode that is working, and neither is a bug.
805	    ///
806	    /// It is COMPUTED rather than a standing warning, which is the whole point
807	    /// of putting it here: it appears only when the trap is really live, and
808	    /// it names which of the two failures the user is looking at. The full
809	    /// explanation, and the answer, live in the popup's tooltip — a note is
810	    /// one truncating line.
811	    ///
812	    /// Read off the FIRST video clip's props, as every other reading in this
813	    /// section is: with a mixed selection the row already shows one clip's
814	    /// value and the mixed badge says the rest disagree.
815	    private func blendNote() -> String? {
816	        let mode = binding.videoProps.blend
817	        guard mode != .normal, let clip = binding.videoClips.first else { return nil }
818	        let snapshot = binding.snapshot
819	        return VideoPane.blendTrapNote(
820	            mode, over: snapshot.canvas.background,
821	            hasLayerBehind: hasVisibleLayerBehind(clip, in: snapshot))
822	    }
823	
824	    /// The note's whole rule, as a function of the three things it depends on
825	    /// — the mode, the canvas colour and whether anything draws underneath —
826	    /// so it can be measured without an inspector around it.
827	    ///
828	    /// **The canvas has to be OPAQUE black, not merely black**, and the alpha
829	    /// is the half the first version left out. `blendPremultiplied`'s
830	    /// `(1 - ab)·src` term carries the source through an empty destination:
831	    /// at `ab` = 0 the whole formula reduces to `src` exactly, for all eight
832	    /// modes — the same property `Compositor+Shadow.swift`'s shadow mask relies on.
833	    /// So over a TRANSPARENT canvas `multiply` renders the layer untouched,
834	    /// and a note reading "multiply reads black here" would name the opposite
835	    /// of what is on screen. Between the two the composite is a partial
836	    /// version of the same (`ab` = 0.5 halves a multiply), which neither verb
837	    /// describes either, so anything short of opaque stands the note down.
838	    /// A missing fourth component reads as 1, which is `RGBA.nsColor`'s
839	    /// convention and the only reading under which a three-component colour
840	    /// means what it says.
841	    static func blendTrapNote(_ mode: BlendMode, over background: RGBA, hasLayerBehind: Bool)
842	        -> String?
843	    {
844	        guard mode != .normal, !hasLayerBehind else { return nil }
845	        // A non-black canvas is something to blend against, so the trap is not
846	        // live: `multiply` over a white canvas is the layer itself, which is
847	        // the identity a person can see and reason about.
848	        guard background.prefix(3).allSatisfy({ $0 <= 0.001 }) else { return nil }
849	        guard background.count > 3 ? background[3] >= 0.999 : true else { return nil }
850	        let collapsesToBlack: Set<BlendMode> = [.multiply, .darken, .overlay]
851	        let verb = collapsesToBlack.contains(mode) ? "reads black here" : "changes nothing here"
852	        return "Nothing behind this clip — \(mode.displayName.lowercased()) \(verb)."
853	    }
854	
855	    /// Whether anything DRAWS under `clip` for any part of its span.
856	    ///
857	    /// Tracks are back-to-front (§6: index 0 is the back), so "behind" is the
858	    /// prefix of the track list before this clip's own, and a hidden track or
859	    /// a clip with its video switched off contributes nothing to blend with.
860	    /// Deliberately a question about the timeline rather than about the frame
861	    /// under the playhead: the note is about the clip, and a blend that has a
862	    /// backdrop for only half its span is not the mistake this warns about.
863	    private func hasVisibleLayerBehind(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot)
864	        -> Bool
865	    {
866	        guard let index = snapshot.tracks.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == clip.track }) else {
867	            return false
868	        }
869	        for track in snapshot.tracks.prefix(index) where !track.hidden {
870	            let covered = snapshot.clips(onTrack: track.id).contains { other in
871	                other.enabled.video && other.start < clip.end && other.end > clip.start
872	            }
873	            if covered { return true }
874	        }
875	        return false
876	    }
877	
878	    /// Fit is `min(cw/sw, ch/sh)`, Fill is `max` (§5.3), centred either way.
879	    /// Each clip gets its own op because the scale depends on ITS source size;
880	    /// clips whose size only the renderer knows (text) are skipped.
881	    private func fitOrFill(fill: Bool) {
882	        let canvas = binding.canvas
883	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
884	        for clip in binding.clips {
885	            guard let source = binding.snapshot.sourceSize(of: clip),
886	                  source.width > 0, source.height > 0
887	            else { continue }
888	            let horizontal = Double(canvas.width) / Double(source.width)
889	            let vertical = Double(canvas.height) / Double(source.height)
890	            let scale = fill ? max(horizontal, vertical) : min(horizontal, vertical)
891	            ops.append(
892	                contentsOf: binding.ops(
893	                    video: VideoPatch(x: 0, y: 0, scale: scale), for: clip))
894	        }
895	        binding.apply(fill ? "Fill Canvas" : "Fit to Canvas", ops)
896	    }
897	}

471	/// and back in just before it (CO-90). After Layout, shut by default.
472	///
473	/// Every row is one undo step "Hide While Silent" and writes the WHOLE gate to
474	/// the base (`structural(video:for:)`: it is not an animation target), each
475	/// edit re-sending the other values as they stand (the Ducking section's
476	/// rule). A gate naming a media whose speech is not saved yet carries that
477	/// media's `set_media_speech` first, in the same step, as Duck by Speech does
478	/// (`DuckSpeech.ops(forMedia:)`); a refusal there sends nothing, and the
479	/// section's note says why.
480	extension VideoPane {
481	
482	    /// Every selected clip draws pixels and none is a nest clip (a nest scope
483	    /// is allowed): a nest clip never draws itself (CO-92).
484	    var allHideable: Bool {
485	        let clips = binding.clips
486	        return !clips.isEmpty
487	            && clips.allSatisfy { clip in
488	                if case .nest = clip.source { return false }
489	                return InspectorTab.hasPixels(clip, in: binding.snapshot)
490	            }
491	    }
492	
493	    func hideSilentSection() -> InspectorSection {
494	        let binding = self.binding
495	        let name = "Hide While Silent"
496	        /// The sentence of the last refused `ops(forMedia:)`, shown as the note.
497	        final class Problem { var text: String? }
498	        let problem = Problem()
499	        func candidates() -> [MediaSnapshot] {
500	            HideSilentSources.candidates(for: binding.clips, in: binding.snapshot)
501	        }
502	        func gated() -> [ClipSnapshot] { binding.videoClips.filter { $0.video?.hideSilent != nil } }
503	        func anyOn() -> Bool { !gated().isEmpty }
504	        func allOn() -> Bool {
505	            !binding.videoClips.isEmpty && gated().count == binding.videoClips.count
506	        }
507	        func current() -> HideSilentProps? { gated().first?.video?.hideSilent }
508	        /// The media's `set_media_speech` ops, or nil when `ops(forMedia:)`
509	        /// refused: then the row writes nothing and the note says why.
510	        func spans(_ media: UInt32) -> [ReelOp]? {
511	            do {
512	                let ops = try DuckSpeech.ops(
513	                    forMedia: media, in: binding.snapshot,
514	                    cacheDirectory: binding.document?.cacheDirectory)
515	                problem.text = nil
516	                return ops
517	            } catch {
518	                problem.text = error.localizedDescription
519	                return nil
520	            }
521	        }
522	        /// The whole gate `next` on every selected picture clip, the spans first.
523	        func write(_ next: HideSilentProps) -> [ReelOp] {
524	            guard let speech = spans(next.media) else { return [] }
525	            return speech + binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(hideSilent: .some(next)))
526	        }
527	        func onOps() -> [ReelOp] {
528	            guard let first = candidates().first else { return [] }
529	            let gate = HideSilentProps(media: first.id)
530	            let set = binding.videoClips.filter { $0.video?.hideSilent == nil }.flatMap {
531	                binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(hideSilent: .some(gate)), for: $0)
532	            }
533	            guard !set.isEmpty, let speech = spans(gate.media) else { return [] }
534	            return speech + set
535	        }
536	        func offOps() -> [ReelOp] { binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(hideSilent: .some(nil))) }
537	        func offerable() -> Bool {
538	            guard let first = candidates().first else { return false }
539	            return DuckSpeech.problem(
540	                forMedia: first.id, in: binding.snapshot,
541	                cacheDirectory: binding.document?.cacheDirectory) == nil
542	        }
543	        /// "Speech from"'s media: the candidates, then the set media when it
544	        /// is not among them.
545	        func sources() -> [MediaSnapshot] {
546	            var list = candidates()
547	            if let set = current()?.media, !list.contains(where: { $0.id == set }),
548	               let row = binding.snapshot.media(set)
549	            {
550	                list.append(row)
551	            }
552	            return list
553	        }
554	        let sourceList = sources()
555	        func seconds(_ ticks: Ticks) -> Double { ReelTime.seconds(ticks) }
556	        func ticks(_ seconds: Double) -> Ticks { ReelTime.ticks(seconds: max(seconds, 0)) }
557	        func edit(_ change: (inout HideSilentProps) -> Void) -> [ReelOp] {
558	            guard var next = current() else { return [] }
559	            change(&next)
560	            return write(next)
561	        }
562	
563	        let check = OptionCheckboxControl(
564	            label: "Hide while silent", read: allOn,
565	            write: { value in binding.apply(name, value ? onOps() : offOps()) },
566	            enabled: { anyOn() || offerable() }, onEdit: { binding.edited() })
567	        if !anyOn(), let first = candidates().first {
568	            check.toolTip = DuckSpeech.problem(
569	                forMedia: first.id, in: binding.snapshot,
570	                cacheDirectory: binding.document?.cacheDirectory)
571	        } else if candidates().isEmpty, !anyOn() {
572	            check.toolTip = "No clip with sound plays under the selection."
573	        }
574	        return InspectorSection(
575	            id: "video.hide_silent", title: "Hide While Silent",
576	            summary: {
577	                guard anyOn() else { return "off" }
578	                let media = Set(gated().map { $0.video?.hideSilent?.media ?? 0 })
579	                guard allOn(), media.count == 1, let id = media.first,
580	                      let row = binding.snapshot.media(id)
581	                else { return "on" }
582	                return row.name
583	            },
584	            note: { problem.text },
585	            reset: { binding.apply(name, offOps()) },
586	            defaultExpanded: false,
587	            rows: [
588	                inspectorRow(
589	                    nil, [check], mixed: { anyOn() && !allOn() }, binding: binding,
590	                    writes: offOps(),
591	                    default: InspectorRowDefault(name: name, differs: anyOn, ops: offOps)),
592	                inspectorPopupRow(
593	                    "Speech from", binding, name: name, items: sourceList.map(\.name),
594	                    read: {
595	                        sourceList.firstIndex { $0.id == current()?.media } ?? 0
596	                    },
597	                    ops: { index in
598	                        guard sourceList.indices.contains(index) else { return [] }
599	                        return edit { $0.media = sourceList[index].id }
600	                    },
601	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.hideSilent?.media } },
602	                    enabled: anyOn, resets: false),
603	                inspectorValueRow(
604	                    "Pre-roll", binding, name: name, unit: " s", decimals: 2, min: 0, max: 5,
605	                    quick: [0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5],
606	                    read: { seconds(current()?.preRoll ?? HideSilentProps.defaultPreRoll) },
607	                    ops: { value in edit { $0.preRoll = ticks(value) } },
608	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.hideSilent?.preRoll } },
609	                    enabled: anyOn),
610	                inspectorValueRow(
611	                    "Hold", binding, name: name, unit: " s", decimals: 2, min: 0, max: 5,
612	                    quick: [0.5, 1, 1.5, 3],
613	                    read: { seconds(current()?.hold ?? HideSilentProps.defaultHold) },
614	                    ops: { value in edit { $0.hold = ticks(value) } },
615	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.hideSilent?.hold } },
616	                    enabled: anyOn),
617	                inspectorValueRow(
618	                    "Fade", binding, name: name, unit: " s", decimals: 2, min: 0, max: 5,
619	                    quick: [0, 0.15, 0.3, 0.5],
620	                    read: { seconds(current()?.fade ?? HideSilentProps.defaultFade) },
621	                    ops: { value in edit { $0.fade = ticks(value) } },
622	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.hideSilent?.fade } },

784	/// end `look: null` only stops animating the look, so it could not remove
