3	/// The Clip tab's **Motion** section (spec §4.3, road map 5's E2) — what a
4	/// clip does on its way in, on its way out, and all the way through.
5	///
6	/// An `extension VideoPane` in a file of its own, `VideoPane+Transition.swift`'s
7	/// shape, because `VideoPane.swift` is over the size cap and may not grow.
8	///
9	/// **Every write is PER CLIP.** A `motion` patch replaces the whole object
10	/// (`MotionProps.dictionary` always writes three keys), so one `set_video`
11	/// over several ids would stamp the first clip's other two slots onto every
12	/// other clip. Each row therefore reads THAT clip's base motion, changes the
13	/// one slot or field, and emits that clip's own op — through
14	/// `ops(video:for:)`, whose `structural` puts motion on the base props even
15	/// inside an action. Reset alone is selection-wide, since every clip gets the
16	/// same value. Reads are the first clip's, the section rule.
17	extension VideoPane {
18	    // MARK: Motion
19	
20	    func motionSection() -> InspectorSection {
21	        let binding = self.binding
22	        let edges = EdgeMotion.allCases
23	        let durings = DuringMotion.allCases
24	        func motion() -> MotionProps { binding.videoProps.motion ?? MotionProps() }
25	        /// One op per clip over the selection's pixel clips; `step` answers
26	        /// the clip's next motion, or nil to skip the clip.
27	        func perClip(_ step: (ClipSnapshot, MotionProps) -> MotionProps?) -> [ReelOp] {
28	            var ops: [ReelOp] = []
29	            for clip in binding.videoClips {
30	                let current = clip.videoProps.motion ?? MotionProps()
31	                guard let next = step(clip, current) else { continue }
32	                ops.append(
33	                    contentsOf: binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(motion: .some(next)), for: clip))
34	            }
35	            return ops
36	        }
37	        func edgeKind(_ index: Int) -> EdgeMotion? {
38	            index == 0 ? nil : edges[min(max(index - 1, 0), edges.count - 1)]
39	        }
40	        /// A chosen kind keeps the slot's stored duration, else the core's
41	        /// own 0.5 s default (`MotionEdge()`).
42	        func edge(_ kind: EdgeMotion?, keeping stored: MotionEdge?) -> MotionEdge? {
43	            guard let kind = kind else { return nil }
44	            return MotionEdge(kind: kind, duration: stored?.duration ?? MotionEdge().duration)
45	        }
46	        func summary() -> String {
47	            let m = motion()
48	            var parts: [String] = []
49	            if let e = m.inEdge { parts.append("in " + e.displayName.lowercased()) }
50	            if let e = m.out { parts.append("out " + e.displayName.lowercased()) }
51	            if let d = m.during { parts.append(d.kind.displayName.lowercased()) }
52	            return parts.isEmpty ? "off" : parts.joined(separator: " · ")
53	        }
54	        func inactiveNote() -> String? {
55	            let selected = binding.videoClips.map { $0.videoProps.motion }
56	            let inactiveIn = selected.contains { $0?.inEdge.map { !$0.isActive } ?? false }
57	            let inactiveOut = selected.contains { $0?.out.map { !$0.isActive } ?? false }
58	            guard inactiveIn || inactiveOut else { return nil }
59	            let slots = [inactiveIn ? "In" : nil, inactiveOut ? "Out" : nil]
60	                .compactMap { $0 }.joined(separator: " and ")
61	            return "Selection includes inactive \(slots) motion (zero duration). "
62	                + "Increase Duration to reactivate; choose None to clear."
63	        }
64	
65	        let preview = commandButton(
66	            "Preview", #selector(EditorViewController.previewClipMotion(_:)),
67	            toolTip:
68	                "Play the clip in a loop: sets the in/out range to the clip and turns Loop on"
69	                + " — both stay until you clear them")
70	
71	        return InspectorSection(
72	            id: "video.motion", title: "Motion presets",
73	            summary: summary,
74	            reset: { binding.apply("Motion", video: VideoPatch(motion: .some(nil))) },
75	            defaultExpanded: false,
76	            rows: [
77	                InspectorNoteLabel(wraps: true, note: inactiveNote),
78	                inspectorPopupRow(
79	                    "In", binding, name: "Motion In", items: ["None"] + edges.map(\.displayName),
80	                    read: { motion().inEdge.map { (edges.firstIndex(of: $0.kind) ?? 0) + 1 } ?? 0 },
81	                    ops: { index in
82	                        perClip { _, m in
83	                            m.with { $0.inEdge = edge(edgeKind(index), keeping: m.inEdge) }
84	                        }
85	                    },
86	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.motion?.inEdge?.kind } }),
87	                // 0.1 s to 10 s: a few frames at the short end, and far longer
88	                // than any entrance is meant to take at the long one.
89	                inspectorValueRow(
90	                    "In Duration", binding, name: "Motion In Duration", unit: " s", decimals: 2,
91	                    min: 0.1, max: 10, quick: [0.25, 0.5, 1], slider: false,
92	                    read: { ReelTime.seconds(motion().inEdge?.duration ?? MotionEdge().duration) },
93	                    ops: { value in
94	                        perClip { _, m in
95	                            guard m.inEdge != nil else { return nil }
96	                            return m.with {
97	                                $0.inEdge?.duration = binding.frameTicks(seconds: value)
98	                            }
99	                        }
100	                    },
101	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.motion?.inEdge?.duration } },
102	                    enabled: { motion().inEdge != nil }),
103	                inspectorPopupRow(
104	                    "Out", binding, name: "Motion Out", items: ["None"] + edges.map(\.displayName),
105	                    read: { motion().out.map { (edges.firstIndex(of: $0.kind) ?? 0) + 1 } ?? 0 },
106	                    ops: { index in
107	                        perClip { _, m in
108	                            m.with { $0.out = edge(edgeKind(index), keeping: m.out) }
109	                        }
110	                    },
111	                    mixed: { binding.mixedVideo { $0.motion?.out?.kind } }),
112	                // The same range as In Duration, for the same reason.
113	                inspectorValueRow(
114	                    "Out Duration", binding, name: "Motion Out Duration", unit: " s", decimals: 2,
115	                    min: 0.1, max: 10, quick: [0.25, 0.5, 1], slider: false,
116	                    read: { ReelTime.seconds(motion().out?.duration ?? MotionEdge().duration) },
117	                    ops: { value in
118	                        perClip { _, m in
119	                            guard m.out != nil else { return nil }
120	                            return m.with { $0.out?.duration = binding.frameTicks(seconds: value) }
121	                        }
122	                    },

124	                    enabled: { motion().out != nil }),
125	                inspectorPopupRow(

128	                    read: {
129	                        motion().during.map { (durings.firstIndex(of: $0.kind) ?? 0) + 1 } ?? 0
130	                    },
131	                    ops: { index in
132	                        perClip { _, m in

182	extension VideoPane {
183	    // MARK: Obscure
184	
185	    /// The obscured regions (§4.3's phase-3c list, schema version 4): boxes
186	    /// on the layer whose contents are blurred or pixelated so a face, a
187	    /// password field or a notification cannot be read.
188	    ///
189	    /// It is the spotlight's inverse and it is spelled in the spotlight's
190	    /// frame — `x`/`y` are the region's CENTRE and `width`/`height` its size,
191	    /// both in SOURCE pixels from the centre of the cropped rect — so a
192	    /// region rides with its layer through scale, move and rotation, and the
193	    /// same four numbers typed into Spotlight put a box in the same place.
194	    /// That is also why the numeric rows are plain px fields rather than
195	    /// percentages, and why a centre outside the layer is allowed.
196	    ///
197	    /// **It is a LIST, so it takes `filtersSection`'s shape and its warning
198	    /// with it.** Nothing here is a general-purpose list editor and it must
199	    /// not become one: the cap is four, so every region is on screen at
200	    /// once; the rows are built against a FIXED INDEX (the count is in
201	    /// `structureSignature`, so add and remove rebuild the pane while
202	    /// dialling a value merely refreshes it); an index the model no longer
203	    /// holds yields the list unchanged, which the core answers as the
204	    /// identity it is; and every write sends the WHOLE array through an
205	    /// ordinary `set_video` patch, which is what keeps add and remove out of
206	    /// the op table (`actions::merge` replaces arrays wholesale).
207	    ///
208	    /// **Adding and removing a region change the CLIP**, not the action under
209	    /// the playhead — including "Place on Canvas", which is an append like
210	    /// any other. A list of a different length in an action's end patch
211	    /// cannot interpolate, so an appended region would be invisible for the
212	    /// whole span and gone at the next write; dialling an existing region's
213	    /// amount or box still belongs to the action, which is what §3c's
214	    /// interpolation rule is for. `InspectorBinding.structural(video:for:)`
215	    /// decides it, for this list and the filter stack alike, and argues it in
216	    /// full.
217	    ///
218	    /// Order does NOT matter here, unlike the filter stack: where two
219	    /// regions overlap the shader takes the STRONGER of them per fragment,
220	    /// so there is no position popup to move a region up or down and the
221	    /// label column carries the region's number instead.
222	    ///
223	    /// **One "Place on Canvas", not one per row.** It appends, and it is
224	    /// disabled at the cap. `InspectorViewController.onCommand` is
225	    /// `(Selector) -> Void` and carries no index (`inspectorCommand` sends a
226	    /// nil sender), so a per-row button would need an index-carrying seam of
227	    /// its own — the first of its kind, added for one button, against the
228	    /// warning above. A region placed on the canvas is edited in its row like
229	    /// any other.
230	    func obscureSection() -> InspectorSection {
231	        let binding = self.binding
232	        let shapes = SpotShape.allCases
233	        let kinds = ObscureKind.allCases
234	        func list() -> [ObscureProps] { binding.videoProps.obscure }
235	        func at(_ index: Int) -> ObscureProps? {
236	            let regions = list()
237	            return regions.indices.contains(index) ? regions[index] : nil
238	        }
239	        func ops(_ next: [ObscureProps]) -> [ReelOp] {
240	            binding.ops(video: VideoPatch(obscure: next))
241	        }
242	        /// The read/write split the filter stack takes, for the same reason
243	        /// and out of the same reader: inside an action a write REPLACES the
244	        /// end patch's array whole, so building it from the interpolated
245	        /// regions would pin every one the user did not touch — and with
246	        /// eight fields a region, seven of them ride along on every edit.
247	        func writeList() -> [ObscureProps] {
248	            binding.editedList(action: { $0.obscure }, base: { $0.obscure })
249	        }
250	        func writeAt(_ index: Int) -> ObscureProps? {
251	            let regions = writeList()
252	            return regions.indices.contains(index) ? regions[index] : nil
253	        }
254	        func replacing(_ index: Int, _ next: ObscureProps) -> [ObscureProps] {
255	            var regions = writeList()
256	            guard regions.indices.contains(index) else { return regions }
257	            regions[index] = next
258	            return regions
259	        }
260	        /// One region with `change` applied, the other fields as they stand —
261	        /// `spotlightSection`'s `edited { … }` over a list. Eight fields is
262	        /// enough that spelling all of them out at every row would bury the
263	        /// one that changes. No change is the region rewritten as it is.
264	        func edited(
265	            _ index: Int, _ change: (inout ObscureProps) -> Void = { _ in }
266	        ) -> [ReelOp] {
267	            // `writeAt`, not `at`: the seven fields that ride along are the
268	            // ones the edit is replacing, never the ones the playhead shows.
269	            guard var o = writeAt(index) else { return [] }
270	            change(&o)
271	            return ops(replacing(index, o))
272	        }
273	        /// The mixed badge for one region's field: a selection where some

275	        func mixedAt<T: Equatable>(_ index: Int, _ read: @escaping (ObscureProps) -> T) -> Bool {
276	            binding.mixedVideo { props in
277	                props.obscure.indices.contains(index) ? read(props.obscure[index]) : nil

279	        }

288	            write: @escaping (Int, Double) -> [ReelOp]
289	        ) -> OptionFieldControl {
290	            OptionFieldControl(
291	                width: InspectorMetrics.fieldWidth, unit: " px", decimals: 0, min: lower,
292	                max: upper, quick: quick,
293	                read: { at(index).map(read) ?? 0 },
294	                write: { value in binding.apply(name, write(index, value)) },
295	                enabled: { true },
296	                onEdit: { binding.edited() })
297	        }
298	
299	        let count = list().count
300	        var rows: [NSView] = []
301	        for index in 0..<count {
302	            let kind = OptionPopupControl(
303	                width: 96, items: kinds.map { $0.displayName },
304	                read: { kinds.firstIndex(of: at(index)?.kind ?? .pixelate) ?? 0 },
305	                write: { choice in

308	                },
309	                enabled: { true },

316	                    guard next.indices.contains(index) else {
317	                        NSSound.beep()

319	                    }
320	                    next.remove(at: index)
321	                    binding.apply("Remove Region", ops(next))
322	                },
323	                enabled: { true }, onEdit: {})
324	            remove.toolTip =
325	                "Take this region off the clip — the clip itself, not the action "
326	                + "under the playhead"
327	            rows.append(
328	                inspectorRow(
329	                    "Region \(index + 1)", [kind, remove],
330	                    mixed: { mixedAt(index) { $0.kind } },
331	                    binding: binding, writes: edited(index)))
332	            rows.append(
333	                inspectorPopupRow(
334	                    "Shape", binding, name: "Obscure Shape",
335	                    items: shapes.map { $0.displayName },
336	                    read: { shapes.firstIndex(of: at(index)?.shape ?? .rect) ?? 0 },
337	                    ops: { choice in
338	                        guard shapes.indices.contains(choice) else { return [] }
339	                        return edited(index) { $0.shape = shapes[choice] }
340	                    },
341	                    mixed: { mixedAt(index) { $0.shape } }))
342	            rows.append(
343	                inspectorValueRow(
344	                    "Amount", binding, name: "Obscure Amount", unit: "%", decimals: 0, min: 0,
345	                    max: 100, quick: [0, 25, 50, 75, 100],
346	                    read: { (at(index)?.amount ?? 0) * 100 },
347	                    ops: { v in edited(index) { $0.amount = v / 100 } },
348	                    mixed: { mixedAt(index) { $0.amount } }))
349	            rows.append(

506	            label: name, read: on,

534	    /// The range's three captioned fields across one row.

536	        _ range: QualifierRange, read: @escaping () -> ColorQualifier,
537	        ops: @escaping (ColorQualifierPatch) -> [ReelOp]
538	    ) -> NSView {
539	        let binding = self.binding
540	        let name = range.title
541	        func on() -> Bool { read().isOn(range) }
542	        typealias Field = (caption: String, max: Double, get: (ColorQualifier) -> Double,
543	                           put: (ColorQualifier, Double) -> ColorQualifierPatch)
544	        let fields: [Field]
545	        if range == .hue {
546	            func hue(_ q: ColorQualifier) -> QualifierHue { q.hue ?? .initial }
547	            fields = [
548	                ("Centre", 360, { hue($0).center },
549	                 { q, v in var h = hue(q); h.center = v; return ColorQualifierPatch(hue: .set(h)) }),
550	                ("Width", 360, { hue($0).width },
551	                 { q, v in var h = hue(q); h.width = v; return ColorQualifierPatch(hue: .set(h)) }),
552	                ("Soft", 180, { hue($0).softness },
553	                 { q, v in var h = hue(q); h.softness = v; return ColorQualifierPatch(hue: .set(h)) }),
554	            ]
555	        } else {
556	            func levels(_ q: ColorQualifier) -> QualifierLevels { q.levels(range) ?? .initial }
557	            fields = [
558	                ("Low", 1, { levels($0).low },
559	                 { q, v in
560	                     var l = levels(q)
561	                     l.low = min(v, l.high)
562	                     return .levels(range, .set(l))
563	                 }),
564	                ("High", 1, { levels($0).high },
565	                 { q, v in
566	                     var l = levels(q)
567	                     l.high = max(v, l.low)
568	                     return .levels(range, .set(l))
569	                 }),
570	                ("Soft", 1, { levels($0).softness },
571	                 { q, v in var l = levels(q); l.softness = v; return .levels(range, .set(l)) }),
572	            ]
573	        }
574	        var controls: [NSView] = []
575	        for field in fields {
576	            let caption = InspectorRowLabel(field.caption)
577	            caption.font = DS.sans(10)
578	            caption.setContentCompressionResistancePriority(.required, for: .horizontal)
579	            controls.append(caption)
580	            controls.append(
581	                OptionFieldControl(
582	                    width: 41, unit: range == .hue ? "°" : "", decimals: range == .hue ? 0 : 2,
583	                    min: 0, max: field.max,
584	                    read: { field.get(read()) },
585	                    write: { [weak binding] value in
586	                        binding?.apply(name, ops(field.put(read(), value)))
587	                    },
588	                    enabled: on,
589	                    onEdit: { [weak binding] in binding?.edited() }))
590	        }
591	        return inspectorRow(nil, controls, binding: binding, writes: ops(.reset))
592	    }

730	/// The Clip tab's **Transition** section (spec §4.3) — the one group that is
731	/// not about the layer's own pixels but about how it MEETS the clip before
732	/// it. `ClipPane` shows it only for a single clip with an overlap
733	/// (`ClipPane.makeSections()`), which is the only state in which an overlap
734	/// has a transition to describe.
735	///
736	/// An `extension VideoPane` in a file of its own because `VideoPane.swift`
737	/// stood at 1465 lines against the ~400-line rule for new files and the
738	/// section is about to grow the Curve popup and the Crossfade Audio check
739	/// row road map 5's E1 adds. The move cost no visibility: `binding` is
740	/// internal and the row builders are free functions.
741	extension VideoPane {
742	    // MARK: Transition
743	
744	    /// The section's five rows: which transition, how it is eased, whether
745	    /// it crossfades the sound and in which shape (format 29, spec §11
746	    /// AU-115; enabled while Crossfade Audio is on), and how long the
747	    /// overlap is.
748	    ///
749	    /// **The Curve and Crossfade Audio rows READ the snapshot's lenient
750	    /// defaults** — `linear` and `false` — which is what a clip with no
751	    /// stored transition draws, and what a version-6 file's transition
752	    /// means. They deliberately do not show what the core would MINT: the
753	    /// section has to say what is there.
754	    ///
755	    /// **And when `transitionIn` is nil, each of the three sends every key.**
756	    /// The Kind popup's index 0 is None, so a clip under an overlap is one
757	    /// click away from having no stored transition at all while still being
758	    /// drawn as a cross dissolve; a one-key `set_transition_style` on that
759	    /// clip would mint `ease_in_out`/`true` underneath and the untouched
760	    /// row would silently change its value. Sending both makes the minted
761	    /// transition exactly what the section was showing, with only the
762	    /// touched value moved. With a transition stored, each row sends its one
763	    /// key and the core keeps the other. `TextPane`'s animation section is
764	    /// the precedent, applied to two scalars rather than to one object.
765	    func transitionSection(_ clip: UInt32) -> InspectorSection {
766	        let binding = self.binding
767	        let kinds = TransitionKind.allCases
768	        let items = ["None"] + kinds.map { $0.displayName }
769	        let curves = Curve.allCases
770	        /// The overlap read fresh: changing the duration MOVES the clip
771	        /// (§6 `set_transition_duration`), so the captured start would be
772	        /// wrong one edit later.
773	        func overlapSeconds() -> Double {
774	            guard let current = binding.snapshot.clip(clip) else { return 0 }
775	            let earlier = binding.snapshot.clips(onTrack: current.track)
776	                .filter { $0.start < current.start }
777	            guard let previous = earlier.last else { return 0 }
778	            return ReelTime.seconds(max(previous.end - current.start, 0))
779	        }
780	        func stored() -> TransitionSnapshot? { binding.snapshot.clip(clip)?.transitionIn }
781	        func curve() -> Curve { stored()?.curve ?? .linear }
782	        func crossfades() -> Bool { stored()?.audio ?? false }
783	        let shapes = FadeShape.allCases
784	        func shape() -> FadeShape { stored()?.audioShape ?? .plus3Db }
785	        /// The style write, carrying the other rows' DISPLAYED values too
786	        /// whenever there is nothing stored to keep them (see the doc above).
787	        func styleOps(curve next: Curve?, audio: Bool?, shape nextShape: FadeShape? = nil)
788	            -> [ReelOp]
789	        {
790	            if stored() == nil {
791	                return [
792	                    .setTransitionStyle(
793	                        clip: clip, curve: next ?? curve(), audio: audio ?? crossfades(),
794	                        audioShape: nextShape ?? shape())
795	                ]
796	            }
797	            return [
798	                .setTransitionStyle(clip: clip, curve: next, audio: audio, audioShape: nextShape)
799	            ]
800	        }
801	        return InspectorSection(
802	            id: "video.transition", title: "Transition",
803	            summary: {
804	                guard let transition = stored() else { return "none" }
805	                return transition.kind.displayName.lowercased()
806	                    + " · " + transition.curve.displayName.lowercased()
807	                    + String(format: " · %.2f s", overlapSeconds())
808	            },
809	            defaultExpanded: false,
810	            rows: [
811	                inspectorPopupRow(
812	                    "Kind", binding, name: "Set Transition", items: items,
813	                    read: {
814	                        guard let kind = binding.snapshot.clip(clip)?.transitionIn?.kind else {
815	                            return 0
816	                        }
817	                        return (kinds.firstIndex(of: kind) ?? 0) + 1
818	                    },
819	                    ops: { index in
820	                        let kind = index == 0 ? nil : kinds[min(max(index - 1, 0), kinds.count - 1)]
821	                        return [.setTransition(clip: clip, kind: kind)]
822	                    }, resets: false),
823	                inspectorPopupRow(
824	                    "Curve", binding, name: "Transition Curve",
825	                    items: curves.map { $0.displayName },
826	                    read: { curves.firstIndex(of: curve()) ?? 0 },
827	                    ops: { index in
828	                        styleOps(
829	                            curve: curves[min(max(index, 0), curves.count - 1)], audio: nil)
830	                    }, resets: false),
831	                inspectorCheckRow(
832	                    "Crossfade Audio", binding, name: "Transition Audio",
833	                    read: crossfades,
834	                    ops: { value in styleOps(curve: nil, audio: value) }, resets: false),
835	                inspectorPopupRow(
836	                    "Crossfade Shape", binding, name: "Crossfade Shape",
837	                    items: shapes.map { $0.title },
838	                    read: { shapes.firstIndex(of: shape()) ?? 0 },
839	                    ops: { index in
840	                        styleOps(
841	                            curve: nil, audio: nil,
842	                            shape: shapes[min(max(index, 0), shapes.count - 1)])
843	                    }, enabled: crossfades, resets: false),
844	                inspectorValueRow(
845	                    "Duration", binding, name: "Transition Duration", unit: " s", decimals: 2,
846	                    min: 0.02, max: 10, quick: [0.25, 0.5, 1, 2], slider: false,
847	                    read: overlapSeconds,
848	                    ops: { value in
849	                        [
850	                            .setTransitionDuration(
851	                                clip: clip,
852	                                duration: binding.frameTicks(seconds: value))
853	                        ]
854	                    }, resets: false),
855	            ])
856	    }

261	    private func loudnessText(gain: Double, limiter: LimiterProps? = nil) -> String {
262	        switch loudnessAnswer() {

264	        case .unavailable: return "—"
265	        case .reading(let reading):

272	    /// One reading's figures at `gain` dB, through `limiter` when there is one.
273	    private func levelText(
274	        lufs measured: Double?, truePeak: Double, steps: [Double], peaks: [Double], gain: Double,
275	        limiter: LimiterProps?
276	    ) -> String {
277	        guard gain.isFinite else { return "silent" }
278	        var peak = truePeak > 0 ? 20 * log10(truePeak) + gain : -.infinity
279	        var lufs = measured.map { $0 + gain }
280	        if let limiter, measured != nil {
281	            let ceiling = pow(10, limiter.ceilingDb / 20)
282	            peak = min(peak, limiter.ceilingDb)
283	            lufs = AudioLimiterModel.integrated(
284	                steps: steps, peaks: peaks, gain: pow(10, gain / 20), ceiling: ceiling,
285	                releaseSeconds: Double(limiter.release) / Double(ReelTime.perSecond))
286	        }
287	        let peakText = peak.isFinite ? String(format: "%.1f dBTP", peak) : "−∞ dBTP"
288	        guard let lufs else { return "— LUFS · " + minus(peakText) }
289	        return minus(String(format: "%.1f LUFS · ", lufs) + peakText)

306	            steps: processed.steps, peaks: processed.peaks, gain: audio.decibels,
307	            limiter: audio.limiter)

309	    }

243	    /// several.

250	    /// Where a relative threshold (or the leveller's target, in `unit`
251	    /// "LUFS") lands for the one selected clip (AU-41), or why the stage is
252	    /// not acting (AU-42); "—" for a selection of several. Short enough for
253	    /// the read-out: "Opens above −51.7 dBFS".
254	    private func dynamicsStatus(
255	        relative: Double, acting: String, idle: String, unit: String = "dBFS"
256	    ) -> String {
257	        switch dynamicsAnswer() {
258	        case nil: return "—"
259	        case .pending: return "Waits for its loudness"
260	        case .unavailable: return "\(idle): no sound"
261	        case .reading(let reading):
262	            guard let lufs = reading.lufs else {
263	                return reading.playedTicks < ClipLoudness.minimumPlayedTicks
264	                    ? "\(idle): too short" : "\(idle): too quiet"
265	            }
266	            return "\(acting) \(AudioPane.decibels(lufs + relative, "%.1f \(unit)"))"
267	        }
268	    }

271	    /// clip: "Aims at −41.7 LUFS" (L + target), "Waits for its loudness",
272	    /// "Waits for its speech", "Not levelling: <reason>"; "—" for several.
273	    private func levellerStatus(target: Double) -> String {
274	        guard binding.isSingle, let clip = binding.primary, let document = binding.document
275	        else { return "—" }
276	        let curves = AudioDynamicsLevels.shared.curves(
277	            for: document.editedProject, cache: document.cacheDirectory)
278	        switch curves[clip.id] {
279	        case nil: return "—"
280	        case .pending(let what): return "Waits for its \(what)"
281	        case .unmeasurable(let reason): return "Not levelling: \(reason)"
282	        case .ready:
283	            return dynamicsStatus(
284	                relative: target, acting: "Aims at", idle: "Not levelling", unit: "LUFS")
285	        }
286	    }

291	        guard case .reading(let reading) = dynamicsAnswer() else {
292	            return dynamicsAnswer() == .pending ? "measuring…" : "—"
293	        }

295	    }

298	        String(format: format, value).replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−")

302	        Ticks((max(milliseconds, 0) / 1000 * Double(ReelTime.perSecond)).rounded())

3	/// The Clip tab's AUDIO sections (spec §4.3): volume with its dB read-out,
4	/// Normalize and mute, the two fades, ducking, voice isolation
5	/// (`AudioPane+Isolation.swift`), the channel pick, the EQ and the hum notch
6	/// (`AudioPane+HumChannels.swift`, `AudioPane+EQ.swift`), noise reduction,
7	/// the compressor, pan, mix-to-mono, Detach Audio and Attach Audio, and the
8	/// limiter (`AudioPane+Limiter.swift`).
9	///
10	/// **This pane is never shown**: since the six tabs became three it is a
11	/// factory `ClipPane` holds and calls, last in the Clip tab, whenever at least
12	/// one selected clip carries audio (`InspectorTab.hasAudio`).
13	///
14	/// Everything here is one `set_audio` patch over the selection, except Detach
15	/// Audio, which is a clip-level op the editor already owns (⌥⌘D) — the pane
16	/// hands it back through `onCommand` rather than re-implementing it — and
17	/// Normalize, which is a `set_audio` PER CLIP because each clip gets its own
18	/// measured gain (`normalize()` says why it cannot go through
19	/// `InspectorBinding.ops(audio:)`).
20	///
21	/// The sections after Ducking are in SIGNAL ORDER rather than in order of
22	/// familiarity: Voice Isolation, Channels, EQ, Hum, noise reduction, the
23	/// compressor, the pan in Mix, then the Limiter, is the order the tap and
24	/// `AudioDSPChain` actually run them in, and the order matters to
25	/// what the numbers mean (the compressor's threshold is read against a signal
26	/// the reducer has already cleaned). Volume, the fades and ducking come first
27	/// in the pane and LAST in the signal, being the fader the core folds into the
28	/// plan's envelope. `ClipPane` keeps them in that order.
29	final class AudioPane: InspectorPaneView {
30	    /// The Volume section's loudness readout (spec §11 AU-15), dropped by a
31	    /// `loudness` cache post.
32	    let loudnessMemo = ClipLoudness.Memo()
33	    /// Voice Isolation's Status read-out (AU-56), dropped by an offline
34	    /// audio settlement.
35	    let isolationMemo = IsolationCache.Memo()
36	    /// Voice Effect's Status read-out (AU-146), dropped with it.
37	    let voiceMemo = IsolationCache.Memo(compute: VoiceCache.status(of:in:))
38	
39	    override init(inspector: InspectorViewController) {
40	        super.init(inspector: inspector)
41	        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
42	            self, selector: #selector(loudnessCacheChanged(_:)), name: .mediaCacheDidChange,
43	            object: nil)
44	        // An isolation render landed or failed (AU-56): Voice Isolation's
45	        // status reads again.
46	        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
47	            self, selector: #selector(offlineAudioSettled(_:)), name: .reversedMediaDidChange,
48	            object: nil)
49	    }
50	
51	    @objc private func offlineAudioSettled(_ note: Notification) {
52	        isolationMemo.invalidate()
53	        voiceMemo.invalidate()
54	        inspector?.refresh(isLive: false)
55	    }
56	
57	    @available(*, unavailable)
58	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
59	        fatalError("AudioPane does not support NSCoder")
60	    }
61	
62	    deinit {
63	        NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(self)
64	    }
65	
66	    /// A loudness file landed or was withdrawn: the memo's files and answers
67	    /// go, and the readout reads again.
68	    @objc private func loudnessCacheChanged(_ note: Notification) {
69	        guard note.userInfo?[MediaImporter.cacheKindKey] as? String == MediaImporter.loudnessKind
70	        else { return }
71	        loudnessMemo.invalidate()
72	        inspector?.refresh(isLive: false)
73	    }

76	
77	    func volumeSection() -> InspectorSection {
78	        let binding = self.binding
79	        // The button lives in Volume rather than in a section of its own: it

133	    /// Normalize Clip's UI half: measure, then commit as ONE undo step, in
134	    /// the mode the Normalize row chose (`NormalizeChoice`, spec §11 AU-15).
135	    ///
136	    /// All of the arithmetic is `AudioNormalize`'s, which is the point — the
137	    /// agent's `normalize_clip` calls the same two functions, so the button and
138	    /// the tool cannot drift apart, and the gains are testable with no window
139	    /// open.
140	    ///
141	    /// It does NOT go through `binding.ops(audio:)`, and that is deliberate.
142	    /// `InspectorBinding.split` does two things every other control here wants
143	    /// and this one must not inherit: it folds every clip outside an action
144	    /// into ONE `set_audio` with many ids and one shared patch — but each clip
145	    /// gets its own measured gain — and it re-routes a clip the playhead is
146	    /// inside an action of into `set_action_end`, where Normalize means the
147	    /// clip's BASE level and never an action's end state. So the ops are built
148	    /// per clip, the shape `SpeedSheetController` already uses for a per-clip
149	    /// computed result.
150	    ///
151	    /// The scope is `normalizable` rather than the raw selection, so a shape,
152	    /// a silent movie or a nest picked alongside is simply not asked about
153	    /// instead of coming back as a refusal the user did not cause.
154	    ///
155	    /// **A run that can normalise nothing beeps**, and so does a second press
156	    /// on an already-normalised selection: `apply` refuses an empty op list,
157	    /// and `ProjectDocument.applyEdit` refuses an identity edit — the recorded
158	    /// consequence `SpeedSheetController` carries for the same reason. The
159	    /// button is not the place that explains WHY a clip was skipped; the tool
160	    /// reports each reason by name under `skipped`.
161	    /// The selected clips Normalize is offered for, which is `audioClips`
162	    /// minus the ones `AudioNormalize` could only refuse.
163	    ///
164	    /// It is not `audioClips` because a NEST is in that list and must not be
165	    /// in this one: a nest clip carrying anything audible has audio properties
166	    /// of its own, so every other control in this section is right to be live
167	    /// on it, but the plan flattens a nest and the clip has no segment — so
168	    /// Normalize on a nest can only beep. `AudioNormalize.canOffer` is the one
169	    /// home of that rule; the Clip menu's validator asks it the same question,
170	    /// or the two would disagree about the same selection.
171	    static func normalizable(_ binding: InspectorBinding) -> [ClipSnapshot] {
172	        binding.audioClips.filter { AudioNormalize.canOffer($0, in: binding.snapshot) }
173	    }

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

246	    /// The one clip the readout is about: exactly one selected clip Normalize
247	    /// is offered for, else nothing ("—").
248	    private var readoutClip: UInt32? {
249	        let clips = AudioPane.normalizable(binding)
250	        return clips.count == 1 && binding.clips.count == 1 ? clips[0].id : nil
251	    }
252	
253	    private func loudnessAnswer() -> ClipLoudness.Answer {
254	        guard let clip = readoutClip, let document = binding.document else { return .unavailable }
255	        return loudnessMemo.answer(for: clip, in: document)
256	    }
257	
258	    /// "−41.7 LUFS · −18.5 dBTP", "measuring…" or "—"; `gain` in dB is added
259	    /// to both (At volume). With `limiter`, the loudness is the model's at that
260	    /// gain and the peak is held at the limiter's ceiling (AU-24, AU-26).
261	    private func loudnessText(gain: Double, limiter: LimiterProps? = nil) -> String {
262	        switch loudnessAnswer() {
263	        case .pending: return "measuring…"
264	        case .unavailable: return "—"
265	        case .reading(let reading):
266	            return levelText(
267	                lufs: reading.lufs, truePeak: reading.truePeak, steps: reading.steps,
268	                peaks: reading.stepPeaks, gain: gain, limiter: limiter)
269	        }
270	    }

272	    /// One reading's figures at `gain` dB, through `limiter` when there is one.
273	    private func levelText(
274	        lufs measured: Double?, truePeak: Double, steps: [Double], peaks: [Double], gain: Double,
275	        limiter: LimiterProps?
276	    ) -> String {
277	        guard gain.isFinite else { return "silent" }
278	        var peak = truePeak > 0 ? 20 * log10(truePeak) + gain : -.infinity
279	        var lufs = measured.map { $0 + gain }
280	        if let limiter, measured != nil {
281	            let ceiling = pow(10, limiter.ceilingDb / 20)
282	            peak = min(peak, limiter.ceilingDb)
283	            lufs = AudioLimiterModel.integrated(
284	                steps: steps, peaks: peaks, gain: pow(10, gain / 20), ceiling: ceiling,
285	                releaseSeconds: Double(limiter.release) / Double(ReelTime.perSecond))
286	        }
287	        let peakText = peak.isFinite ? String(format: "%.1f dBTP", peak) : "−∞ dBTP"
288	        guard let lufs else { return "— LUFS · " + minus(peakText) }
289	        return minus(String(format: "%.1f LUFS · ", lufs) + peakText)
290	    }

292	    /// At volume (spec §11 AU-64 (g)): on a clip whose chain has a stage the
293	    /// loudness cache leaves out, the last R0 measured for its plan and chain
294	    /// (`ProcessedLoudness.Memo`) at the current volume and limiter, else the
295	    /// cache figure marked approximate; any other clip, the cache figure.
296	    private func atVolumeText(_ audio: AudioProps) -> (text: String, approximate: Bool) {
297	        let cached = loudnessText(gain: audio.decibels, limiter: audio.limiter)
298	        guard ProcessedLoudness.needsRender(audio), let clip = readoutClip,
299	            let document = binding.document, case .reading = loudnessAnswer()

301	        guard let processed = ProcessedLoudness.Memo.shared.reading(for: clip, in: document) else {
302	            return ("≈ " + cached, true)
303	        }
304	        let text = levelText(
305	            lufs: StepLoudness.integrated(processed.steps), truePeak: processed.peaks.max() ?? 0,
306	            steps: processed.steps, peaks: processed.peaks, gain: audio.decibels,
307	            limiter: audio.limiter)
308	        return (text, false)
309	    }

250	    /// Where a relative threshold (or the leveller's target, in `unit`
251	    /// "LUFS") lands for the one selected clip (AU-41), or why the stage is
252	    /// not acting (AU-42); "—" for a selection of several. Short enough for
253	    /// the read-out: "Opens above −51.7 dBFS".
254	    private func dynamicsStatus(
255	        relative: Double, acting: String, idle: String, unit: String = "dBFS"
256	    ) -> String {
257	        switch dynamicsAnswer() {
258	        case nil: return "—"
259	        case .pending: return "Waits for its loudness"
260	        case .unavailable: return "\(idle): no sound"
261	        case .reading(let reading):
262	            guard let lufs = reading.lufs else {
263	                return reading.playedTicks < ClipLoudness.minimumPlayedTicks
264	                    ? "\(idle): too short" : "\(idle): too quiet"
265	            }
266	            return "\(acting) \(AudioPane.decibels(lufs + relative, "%.1f \(unit)"))"
267	        }
268	    }

273	    private func levellerStatus(target: Double) -> String {
274	        guard binding.isSingle, let clip = binding.primary, let document = binding.document
275	        else { return "—" }
276	        let curves = AudioDynamicsLevels.shared.curves(
277	            for: document.editedProject, cache: document.cacheDirectory)
278	        switch curves[clip.id] {
279	        case nil: return "—"
280	        case .pending(let what): return "Waits for its \(what)"
281	        case .unmeasurable(let reason): return "Not levelling: \(reason)"
282	        case .ready:
283	            return dynamicsStatus(
284	                relative: target, acting: "Aims at", idle: "Not levelling", unit: "LUFS")
285	        }

297	    private static func decibels(_ value: Double, _ format: String) -> String {
298	        String(format: format, value).replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−")

302	        Ticks((max(milliseconds, 0) / 1000 * Double(ReelTime.perSecond)).rounded())

4	/// Normalize and mute, the two fades, ducking, voice isolation
5	/// (`AudioPane+Isolation.swift`), the channel pick, the EQ and the hum notch
6	/// (`AudioPane+HumChannels.swift`, `AudioPane+EQ.swift`), noise reduction,
7	/// the compressor, pan, mix-to-mono, Detach Audio and Attach Audio, and the
8	/// limiter (`AudioPane+Limiter.swift`).
9	///
10	/// **This pane is never shown**: since the six tabs became three it is a
11	/// factory `ClipPane` holds and calls, last in the Clip tab, whenever at least
12	/// one selected clip carries audio (`InspectorTab.hasAudio`).
13	///
14	/// Everything here is one `set_audio` patch over the selection, except Detach
15	/// Audio, which is a clip-level op the editor already owns (⌥⌘D) — the pane
16	/// hands it back through `onCommand` rather than re-implementing it — and
17	/// Normalize, which is a `set_audio` PER CLIP because each clip gets its own
18	/// measured gain (`normalize()` says why it cannot go through
19	/// `InspectorBinding.ops(audio:)`).
20	///
21	/// The sections after Ducking are in SIGNAL ORDER rather than in order of
22	/// familiarity: Voice Isolation, Channels, EQ, Hum, noise reduction, the
23	/// compressor, the pan in Mix, then the Limiter, is the order the tap and
24	/// `AudioDSPChain` actually run them in, and the order matters to
25	/// what the numbers mean (the compressor's threshold is read against a signal
26	/// the reducer has already cleaned). Volume, the fades and ducking come first
27	/// in the pane and LAST in the signal, being the fader the core folds into the
28	/// plan's envelope. `ClipPane` keeps them in that order.

133	    /// Normalize Clip's UI half: measure, then commit as ONE undo step, in
134	    /// the mode the Normalize row chose (`NormalizeChoice`, spec §11 AU-15).
135	    ///
136	    /// All of the arithmetic is `AudioNormalize`'s, which is the point — the
137	    /// agent's `normalize_clip` calls the same two functions, so the button and
138	    /// the tool cannot drift apart, and the gains are testable with no window
139	    /// open.
140	    ///
141	    /// It does NOT go through `binding.ops(audio:)`, and that is deliberate.
142	    /// `InspectorBinding.split` does two things every other control here wants
143	    /// and this one must not inherit: it folds every clip outside an action
144	    /// into ONE `set_audio` with many ids and one shared patch — but each clip
145	    /// gets its own measured gain — and it re-routes a clip the playhead is
146	    /// inside an action of into `set_action_end`, where Normalize means the
147	    /// clip's BASE level and never an action's end state. So the ops are built
148	    /// per clip, the shape `SpeedSheetController` already uses for a per-clip
149	    /// computed result.
150	    ///
151	    /// The scope is `normalizable` rather than the raw selection, so a shape,
152	    /// a silent movie or a nest picked alongside is simply not asked about
153	    /// instead of coming back as a refusal the user did not cause.
154	    ///
155	    /// **A run that can normalise nothing beeps**, and so does a second press
156	    /// on an already-normalised selection: `apply` refuses an empty op list,
157	    /// and `ProjectDocument.applyEdit` refuses an identity edit — the recorded
158	    /// consequence `SpeedSheetController` carries for the same reason. The
159	    /// button is not the place that explains WHY a clip was skipped; the tool
160	    /// reports each reason by name under `skipped`.
161	    /// The selected clips Normalize is offered for, which is `audioClips`
162	    /// minus the ones `AudioNormalize` could only refuse.
163	    ///
164	    /// It is not `audioClips` because a NEST is in that list and must not be
165	    /// in this one: a nest clip carrying anything audible has audio properties
166	    /// of its own, so every other control in this section is right to be live
167	    /// on it, but the plan flattens a nest and the clip has no segment — so
168	    /// Normalize on a nest can only beep. `AudioNormalize.canOffer` is the one
169	    /// home of that rule; the Clip menu's validator asks it the same question,
170	    /// or the two would disagree about the same selection.
171	    static func normalizable(_ binding: InspectorBinding) -> [ClipSnapshot] {
172	        binding.audioClips.filter { AudioNormalize.canOffer($0, in: binding.snapshot) }
173	    }

238	    /// "Lower other audio to N % while this clip plays" — by the clip's

240	    /// while its speech plays, widened by Pre-roll and Hold. The core folds
241	    /// either into the other clips' envelopes.
242	    ///
243	    /// Every control writes a whole `DuckProps`: the patch replaces the
244	    /// object, so each edit re-sends the other values as they stand.
245	    /// Attack, release, pre-roll and hold are stored as typed, off the frame
246	    /// grid (§11 #355).
247	    ///
248	    /// **Choosing Speech is ONE edit with the spans** (AU-111): the
249	    /// `set_media_speech` each media without spans needs, from its voice
250	    /// cache (`DuckSpeech.ops`), then the `set_audio`. Every other duck edit
251	    /// re-sends `mode`, so on a Speech duck it carries the same spans first,
252	    /// as `AgentServer.setAudio` does: a Level edit on a pasted spanless
253	    /// Speech duck saves its media's spans and applies. A media whose cache
254	    /// cannot be read adds none, and the core refuses the edit in its own
255	    /// sentence rather than the row doing nothing. Speech cannot be chosen

266	                for: binding.audioClips, in: binding.snapshot,
267	                cacheDirectory: binding.document?.cacheDirectory)) ?? []
268	            return spans + set
269	        }
270	        func on() -> Bool { binding.audioProps.duck != nil }
271	        func speech() -> Bool { on() && current().mode == .speech }
272	        func offerable() -> Bool {
273	            speech()
274	                || DuckSpeech.problem(
275	                    for: binding.audioClips, in: binding.snapshot,
276	                    cacheDirectory: binding.document?.cacheDirectory) == nil
277	        }

364	    ///
365	    /// The read-out states the strongest attenuation any part of the spectrum
366	    /// can receive, which is the one number that describes this honestly: the
367	    /// filter is a spectral attenuator over a noise floor it measures from the
368	    /// clip itself, so it never removes MORE than the floor it found, and the
369	    /// amount sets how far a bin may be pushed down. It is not a gate and does
370	    /// not silence anything between words; see
371	    /// `AudioNoiseReductionStage` for what it does, sample by sample.

413	    /// (`rampTicks`, §11 #355). A compressor's attack is 10 ms where a frame

417	        let binding = self.binding
418	        func current() -> CompressorProps { binding.audioProps.compressor ?? CompressorProps() }
419	        func ops(_ next: CompressorProps) -> [ReelOp] {
420	            binding.ops(audio: AudioPatch(compressor: .some(next)))
421	        }
422	        func on() -> Bool { binding.audioProps.compressor != nil }
423	        func ticks(_ milliseconds: Double) -> Ticks {
424	            Ticks((max(milliseconds, 0) / 1000 * Double(ReelTime.perSecond)).rounded())
425	        }
426	        func milliseconds(_ ticks: Ticks) -> Double {
427	            Double(ticks) / Double(ReelTime.perSecond) * 1000
428	        }
429	        return InspectorSection(
430	            id: "audio.compressor", title: "Compressor",
431	            summary: { on() ? String(format: "%.1f:1", current().ratio) : "off" },
432	            reset: { binding.apply("Compressor", audio: AudioPatch(compressor: .some(nil))) },
433	            defaultExpanded: false,
434	            rows: [
435	                inspectorCheckRow(
436	                    "Smooth volume levels", binding, name: "Compressor",
437	                    read: on,
438	                    ops: { value in
439	                        binding.ops(
440	                            audio: AudioPatch(
441	                                compressor: value ? .some(CompressorProps()) : .some(nil)))
442	                    },
443	                    mixed: { binding.mixedAudio { $0.compressor != nil } }),
444	                inspectorValueRow(
445	                    "Threshold", binding, name: "Compressor Threshold", unit: " dB", decimals: 1,
446	                    min: -60, max: 0, quick: [-30, -24, -18, -12, -6],
447	                    read: { current().thresholdDb },
448	                    ops: { value in
449	                        var c = current()
450	                        c.thresholdDb = value
451	                        return ops(c)
452	                    },
453	                    mixed: { binding.mixedAudio { $0.compressor?.thresholdDb } },
454	                    enabled: on),
455	                inspectorValueRow(
456	                    "Ratio", binding, name: "Compressor Ratio", unit: ":1", decimals: 1, min: 1,
457	                    max: 20, quick: [1.5, 2, 3, 4, 8, 20],
458	                    read: { current().ratio },
459	                    ops: { value in
460	                        var c = current()
461	                        c.ratio = value
462	                        return ops(c)
463	                    },
464	                    mixed: { binding.mixedAudio { $0.compressor?.ratio } },
465	                    enabled: on),
466	                inspectorValueRow(
467	                    "Attack", binding, name: "Compressor Attack", unit: " ms", decimals: 0, min: 0,
468	                    max: 200, quick: [1, 5, 10, 30, 100],
469	                    read: { milliseconds(current().attack) },
470	                    ops: { value in
471	                        var c = current()
472	                        c.attack = ticks(value)
473	                        return ops(c)
474	                    },
475	                    mixed: { binding.mixedAudio { $0.compressor?.attack } },
476	                    enabled: on),
477	                inspectorValueRow(
478	                    "Release", binding, name: "Compressor Release", unit: " ms", decimals: 0,
479	                    min: 10, max: 2000, quick: [50, 100, 200, 500, 1000],
480	                    read: { milliseconds(current().release) },
481	                    ops: { value in
482	                        var c = current()
483	                        c.release = ticks(value)
484	                        return ops(c)
485	                    },
486	                    mixed: { binding.mixedAudio { $0.compressor?.release } },
487	                    enabled: on),
488	                inspectorValueRow(
489	                    "Makeup", binding, name: "Compressor Makeup", unit: " dB", decimals: 1, min: 0,
490	                    max: 24, quick: [0, 3, 6, 12],
491	                    read: { current().makeupDb },
492	                    ops: { value in
493	                        var c = current()
494	                        c.makeupDb = value
495	                        return ops(c)
496	                    },
497	                    mixed: { binding.mixedAudio { $0.compressor?.makeupDb } },
498	                    enabled: on),
499	            ])

503	
504	    /// Pan lives here rather than in a section of its own because it is a
505	    /// placement control, next to the other one.
506	    ///
507	    /// It is a BALANCE on a stereo clip — one gain per channel, unity at the
508	    /// centre, constant power across the sweep (`AudioPanLaw`) — and it is
509	    /// inaudible on a clip whose source is mono, because the widening to
510	    /// stereo happens after the point where the pan is applied. The read-out
511	    /// says which side, so "0" is never ambiguous.
512	    func mixSection() -> InspectorSection {

519	            toolTip: "Merge a detached sound back into its picture (⇧⌥⌘D)")
520	        return InspectorSection(
521	            id: "audio.mix", title: "Mix",
522	            summary: {
523	                let pan = binding.audioProps.pan
524	                if abs(pan) < 0.005 { return binding.audioProps.mono ? "mono" : "centre" }
525	                return String(format: "%@ %.0f", pan < 0 ? "left" : "right", abs(pan) * 100)
526	            },

528	            defaultExpanded: false,
529	            rows: [
530	                inspectorValueRow(
531	                    "Pan", binding, name: "Pan", unit: "", decimals: 0, min: -100, max: 100,
532	                    quick: [-100, -50, 0, 50, 100],
533	                    read: { binding.audioProps.pan * 100 },
534	                    ops: { binding.ops(audio: AudioPatch(pan: $0 / 100)) },
535	                    mixed: { binding.mixedAudio { $0.pan } }),
536	                inspectorRow(
537	                    "Position",
538	                    [
539	                        inspectorReadout {
540	                            let pan = binding.audioProps.pan
541	                            if abs(pan) < 0.005 { return "centre" }
542	                            return String(

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

1	import AppKit

3	/// The Clip tab's TEXT sections (spec §4.3): content, face, colour,
4	/// alignment, spacing, outline, backdrop, the box mode, how the words arrive
5	/// and leave, and the four presets.
6	///
7	/// **This pane is never shown**: since the six tabs became three it is a
8	/// factory `ClipPane` holds and calls, right after Transform, when EVERY
9	/// selected clip is a text clip. Shadow is not in the list any more — it is
10	/// one field (`video.shadow`) shared with the video and shape sections, so the
11	/// Clip tab carries it once, in the effects group.
12	///
13	/// The model stores ONE font string — a PostScript name (§5.2's
14	/// `"SourceSans3-SemiBold"`) — while the panel offers the two popups people
15	/// expect, family and style. `TextFace` is the whole translation between
16	/// them, and it is deliberately tolerant: a project made on another machine
17	/// can name a face this one does not have, and the pane must still open.
18	final class TextPane: InspectorPaneView {
19	    /// Whether the text sections apply: they write `set_text`, which errors on
20	    /// any other kind, so a mixed selection gets none of them.
21	    var allText: Bool {
22	        !binding.clips.isEmpty && binding.textClips.count == binding.clips.count
23	    }
24	
25	    /// A family change replaces the style popup's ITEMS, so it has to be part
26	    /// of the rebuild signature — refreshing alone would leave the old
27	    /// family's styles listed.
28	    override var structureSignature: String {
29	        super.structureSignature + "|" + TextFace.family(of: binding.textProps.font)
30	    }
31	
32	    // MARK: Content
33	
34	    /// The footnote on a word-styled page whose timings a content edit
35	    /// dropped (road map 8 §5e), and the Animation section's on a styled
36	    /// page, whose reveal the word style replaces (spec §11 W-5). The second
37	    /// is short on purpose: its row is 244 pt at the 280 pt narrowest
38	    /// inspector (`DocumentPane.transparencyNote` has the arithmetic, #70).
39	    static let untimedNote = "Not timed — regenerate to time it again"
40	    static let wordStyleNote = "Word style wins; the reveal does not apply."
41	
42	    func contentSection() -> InspectorSection {
43	        let binding = self.binding
44	        let area = InspectorTextArea(
45	            read: { binding.textProps.content },
46	            // Per clip: a timed page keeps its words while the count holds
47	            // and sends `words: []` beside the content when it does not.
48	            write: { value in binding.apply("Edit Text", binding.ops(textContent: value)) },
49	            enabled: { !binding.textClips.isEmpty },
50	            onEdit: { binding.edited() })
51	        return InspectorSection(
52	            id: "text.content", title: "Content",
53	            summary: {
54	                let line = binding.textProps.content
55	                    .split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).first.map(String.init) ?? ""
56	                return line.isEmpty ? "empty" : line
57	            },
58	            note: {
59	                binding.textProps.isUntimedPage ? Self.untimedNote : nil
60	            },
61	            rows: [inspectorRow(nil, [area], binding: binding,
62	                                writes: binding.ops(textContent: binding.textProps.content),
63	                                discrete: true)])
64	    }
65	
66	    // MARK: Face
67	
68	    func fontSection() -> InspectorSection {
69	        let binding = self.binding
70	        let families = TextFace.families
71	        let family = TextFace.family(of: binding.textProps.font)
72	        let members = TextFace.members(of: family)
73	        let font = binding.ops(text: TextPatch(font: binding.textProps.font))
74	
75	        let familyPopup = OptionPopupControl(
76	            width: 150, items: families,
77	            read: { families.firstIndex(of: TextFace.family(of: binding.textProps.font)) ?? 0 },
78	            write: { index in
79	                guard families.indices.contains(index) else { return }
80	                let current = binding.textProps.font
81	                let name = TextFace.postScriptName(
82	                    family: families[index], style: TextFace.style(of: current))
83	                binding.apply("Font", text: TextPatch(font: name))
84	            },
85	            enabled: { true },
86	            onEdit: { binding.edited() })
87	
88	        let stylePopup = OptionPopupControl(
89	            width: 116, items: members.map { $0.style },
90	            read: {
91	                let name = binding.textProps.font
92	                return members.firstIndex { $0.name == name } ?? 0
93	            },
94	            write: { index in
95	                guard members.indices.contains(index) else { return }
96	                binding.apply("Font", text: TextPatch(font: members[index].name))
97	            },
98	            enabled: { !members.isEmpty },
99	            onEdit: { binding.edited() })
100	
101	        return InspectorSection(
102	            id: "text.font", title: "Font",
103	            summary: { String(format: "%.0f px", binding.textProps.size) },
104	            defaultExpanded: false,
105	            rows: [
106	                inspectorRow(
107	                    "Family", [familyPopup], mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.font } },
108	                    binding: binding, writes: font),
109	                inspectorRow("Style", [stylePopup], binding: binding, writes: font),
110	                inspectorValueRow(
111	                    "Size", binding, name: "Font Size", unit: " px", decimals: 0, min: 6,
112	                    max: 800, quick: [24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 144], slider: false,
113	                    read: { binding.textProps.size },
114	                    ops: { binding.ops(text: TextPatch(size: $0)) },
115	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.size } }),
116	            ])
117	    }
118	
119	    // MARK: Style
120	
121	    func styleSection() -> InspectorSection {
122	        let binding = self.binding
123	        let aligns = ["left", "center", "right"]
124	        let valigns = ["top", "middle", "bottom"]
125	        let text = binding.textProps
126	        let align = OptionSegmentedControl(
127	            segments: [
128	                ("text.alignleft", "L", "Align left"),
129	                ("text.aligncenter", "C", "Align center"),
130	                ("text.alignright", "R", "Align right"),
131	            ],
132	            read: { aligns.firstIndex(of: binding.textProps.align) ?? 1 },
133	            write: { index in
134	                guard aligns.indices.contains(index) else { return }
135	                binding.apply("Alignment", text: TextPatch(align: aligns[index]))
136	            },
137	            segmentEnabled: nil, enabled: { true },
138	            onEdit: { binding.edited() })
139	        let valign = OptionSegmentedControl(
140	            segments: [
141	                ("align.vertical.top", "⤒", "Align to the top of the box"),
142	                ("align.vertical.center", "↕", "Center in the box"),
143	                ("align.vertical.bottom", "⤓", "Align to the bottom of the box"),
144	            ],
145	            read: { valigns.firstIndex(of: binding.textProps.valign) ?? 1 },
146	            write: { index in
147	                guard valigns.indices.contains(index) else { return }
148	                binding.apply("Alignment", text: TextPatch(valign: valigns[index]))
149	            },
150	            segmentEnabled: nil, enabled: { true },
151	            onEdit: { binding.edited() })
152	
153	        return InspectorSection(
154	            id: "text.style", title: "Style",
155	            summary: { binding.textProps.align },
156	            reset: {
157	                let defaults = TextProps()
158	                binding.apply(
159	                    "Text Style",
160	                    text: TextPatch(
161	                        color: defaults.color, align: defaults.align, valign: defaults.valign,
162	                        lineSpacing: defaults.lineSpacing, tracking: defaults.tracking,
163	                        textCase: defaults.textCase))
164	            },
165	            defaultExpanded: false,
166	            rows: [
167	                inspectorColorRow(
168	                    "Color", binding, name: "Text Color", read: { binding.textProps.color },
169	                    ops: { binding.ops(text: TextPatch(color: $0)) },
170	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.color } }),
171	                inspectorRow("Align", [align], mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.align } },
172	                    binding: binding, writes: binding.ops(text: TextPatch(align: text.align)),
173	                    default: .derived(binding, name: "Alignment", read: { binding.textProps.align },
174	                                      ops: { binding.ops(text: TextPatch(align: $0)) })),
175	                inspectorRow("Vertical", [valign], mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.valign } },
176	                    binding: binding, writes: binding.ops(text: TextPatch(valign: text.valign)),
177	                    default: .derived(
178	                        binding, name: "Alignment", read: { binding.textProps.valign },
179	                        ops: { binding.ops(text: TextPatch(valign: $0)) })),
180	                inspectorCheckRow(
181	                    "UPPERCASE", binding, name: "Case",
182	                    read: { binding.textProps.textCase == .upper },
183	                    ops: { binding.ops(text: TextPatch(textCase: $0 ? .upper : .asWritten)) },
184	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.textCase } }),
185	                inspectorValueRow(
186	                    "Line spacing", binding, name: "Line Spacing", unit: "×", decimals: 2,
187	                    min: 0.5, max: 4,
188	                    read: { binding.textProps.lineSpacing },
189	                    ops: { binding.ops(text: TextPatch(lineSpacing: $0)) },
190	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.lineSpacing } }),
191	                inspectorValueRow(
192	                    "Tracking", binding, name: "Tracking", unit: " px", decimals: 1, min: -20,
193	                    max: 100,
194	                    read: { binding.textProps.tracking },
195	                    ops: { binding.ops(text: TextPatch(tracking: $0)) },
196	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.tracking } }),
197	            ])
198	    }

201	
202	    func outlineSection() -> InspectorSection {
203	        let binding = self.binding
204	        func current() -> OutlineProps { binding.textProps.outline ?? OutlineProps() }
205	        func on() -> Bool { binding.textProps.outline != nil }
206	        return InspectorSection(
207	            id: "text.outline", title: "Outline",
208	            summary: { on() ? String(format: "%.1f px", current().width) : "off" },
209	            reset: { binding.apply("Outline", text: TextPatch(outline: .some(nil))) },
210	            defaultExpanded: false,
211	            rows: [
212	                inspectorCheckRow(
213	                    "Outline", binding, name: "Outline", read: on,
214	                    ops: { value in
215	                        binding.ops(
216	                            text: TextPatch(outline: value ? .some(OutlineProps()) : .some(nil)))
217	                    },
218	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.outline != nil } }),
219	                inspectorValueRow(
220	                    "Width", binding, name: "Outline Width", unit: " px", decimals: 1, min: 0,
221	                    max: 40, quick: [1, 2, 4, 8],
222	                    read: { current().width },
223	                    ops: { value in
224	                        var o = current()
225	                        o.width = value
226	                        return binding.ops(text: TextPatch(outline: .some(o)))
227	                    },
228	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.outline?.width } },
229	                    enabled: on),
230	                inspectorColorRow(
231	                    "Color", binding, name: "Outline Color", read: { current().color },
232	                    ops: { color in
233	                        var o = current()
234	                        o.color = color
235	                        return binding.ops(text: TextPatch(outline: .some(o)))
236	                    },
237	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.outline?.color } },
238	                    enabled: on),
239	            ])
240	    }
