242	    // MARK: Backdrop
243	
244	    func backdropSection() -> InspectorSection {
245	        let binding = self.binding
246	        func current() -> BackdropProps { binding.textProps.backdrop ?? BackdropProps() }
247	        func on() -> Bool { binding.textProps.backdrop != nil }
248	        func ops(_ next: BackdropProps) -> [ReelOp] {
249	            binding.ops(text: TextPatch(backdrop: .some(next)))
250	        }
251	        return InspectorSection(
252	            id: "text.backdrop", title: "Backdrop",
253	            summary: { on() ? String(format: "%.0f px", current().padding) : "off" },
254	            reset: { binding.apply("Backdrop", text: TextPatch(backdrop: .some(nil))) },
255	            defaultExpanded: false,
256	            rows: [
257	                inspectorCheckRow(
258	                    "Backdrop", binding, name: "Backdrop", read: on,

340	
341	    /// How the words arrive and how they leave (§4.3, format version 5).
342	    ///
343	    /// Three controls for three keys: which reveal, how long it takes to
344	    /// arrive, and how long it takes to leave. The core turns them into one
345	    /// number per frame — nothing here draws or times anything, and the
346	    /// section cannot show the reveal's progress, because the progress is a
347	    /// fact about the frame under the playhead and not about the clip.
348	    ///
349	    /// `animation` is a whole OBJECT in the patch, so every row re-sends all
350	    /// three keys. The core MERGES a nested object key by key (§5.2), but a
351	    /// stored `null` is not an object — turning the reveal ON replaces the
352	    /// null with what this patch carries, and a key left out would then come
353	    /// from the struct's default and silently reset what the user did not
354	    /// touch. A section that knows all three keys is right in both cases.
355	    /// Turning the popup to None sends an explicit null, which is the
356	    /// model's "no animation".
357	    ///
358	    /// One thing worth knowing before animating this section from an action:
359	    /// `in` and `out` are numbers, so an action END patch would interpolate
360	    /// them and slide the animation's own timebase mid-reveal. The kind is a
361	    /// string and switches at the end, which is the sane half.
362	    func animationSection() -> InspectorSection {
363	        let binding = self.binding
364	        let kinds = TextAnimationKind.allCases
365	        let items = ["None"] + kinds.map { $0.displayName }
366	        func current() -> TextAnimation { binding.textProps.animation ?? TextAnimation() }
367	        func on() -> Bool { binding.textProps.animation != nil }
368	        func free() -> Bool { binding.textProps.wordStyle == nil }
369	        func ops(_ next: TextAnimation) -> [ReelOp] {
370	            binding.ops(text: TextPatch(animation: .some(next)))
371	        }
372	        return InspectorSection(
373	            id: "text.animation", title: "Reveal",
374	            summary: {
375	                guard let animation = binding.textProps.animation else { return "off" }
376	                return animation.kind.displayName.lowercased()
377	                    + String(format: " · %.2f s", ReelTime.seconds(animation.inDuration))
378	            },
379	            note: { free() ? nil : Self.wordStyleNote },
380	            reset: { binding.apply("Animation", text: TextPatch(animation: .some(nil))) },
381	            defaultExpanded: false,
382	            rows: [
383	                inspectorPopupRow(
384	                    "Reveal", binding, name: "Text Animation", items: items,
385	                    read: {
386	                        guard let kind = binding.textProps.animation?.kind else { return 0 }
387	                        return (kinds.firstIndex(of: kind) ?? 0) + 1
388	                    },
389	                    ops: { index in
390	                        guard index > 0, kinds.indices.contains(index - 1) else {
391	                            return binding.ops(text: TextPatch(animation: .some(nil)))
392	                        }
393	                        // The durations as they stand: switching the reveal
394	                        // must not reset the timing the user chose for it.
395	                        var a = current()
396	                        a.kind = kinds[index - 1]
397	                        return ops(a)
398	                    },
399	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.animation?.kind } }, enabled: free),
400	                inspectorValueRow(
401	                    "In", binding, name: "Animation In", unit: " s", decimals: 2, min: 0, max: 10,
402	                    quick: [0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2],
403	                    read: { ReelTime.seconds(current().inDuration) },
404	                    ops: { value in
405	                        var a = current()
406	                        a.inDuration = binding.frameTicks(seconds: value)
407	                        return ops(a)
408	                    },
409	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.animation?.inDuration } },
410	                    enabled: { on() && free() }),
411	                inspectorValueRow(
412	                    "Out", binding, name: "Animation Out", unit: " s", decimals: 2, min: 0,
413	                    max: 10, quick: [0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2],
414	                    read: { ReelTime.seconds(current().outDuration) },
415	                    ops: { value in
416	                        var a = current()
417	                        a.outDuration = binding.frameTicks(seconds: value)
418	                        return ops(a)
419	                    },
420	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.animation?.outDuration } },
421	                    enabled: { on() && free() }),
422	            ])

459	/// One text preset (§4.3). Sizes and positions are FRACTIONS of the canvas so
460	/// a preset means the same thing on a 4K canvas as on a vertical one: a size
461	/// of the canvas's SHORT side, a position of its width and height (spec §11
462	/// VR-41), so a tall canvas gets the line height a wide one has.
463	struct TextPreset {
464	    let name: String
465	    let font: String
466	    let sizeFraction: Double
467	    let xFraction: Double
468	    let yFraction: Double
469	    let align: String
470	    let backdrop: BackdropProps?
471	    /// Of H, on a canvas taller than wide, in place of `yFraction` (the Caption
472	    /// row's 0.25, VR-41); nil keeps `yFraction` on every canvas.
473	    var tallYFraction: Double? = nil
474	
475	    /// The font size on `canvas`: `sizeFraction` of `min(W, H)`. On a canvas at
476	    /// least as wide as tall that is H, so the old `H × sizeFraction` is kept to the bit.
477	    func size(on canvas: CGSize) -> Double {
478	        (sizeFraction * Double(min(canvas.width, canvas.height))).rounded()
479	    }
480	
481	    /// Where the box's centre sits on `canvas`.
482	    func position(on canvas: CGSize) -> (x: Double, y: Double) {
483	        let y = canvas.height > canvas.width ? tallYFraction ?? yFraction : yFraction
484	        return (xFraction * Double(canvas.width), y * Double(canvas.height))
485	    }
486	
487	    /// Text ▸ Presets' two patches: the face, size, alignment and backdrop, and where the
488	    /// box sits at full opacity.
489	    func patches(on canvas: CGSize) -> (text: TextPatch, video: VideoPatch) {
490	        let at = position(on: canvas)
491	        return (
492	            TextPatch(
493	                font: font, size: size(on: canvas), align: align, valign: "middle",
494	                backdrop: .some(backdrop)),
495	            VideoPatch(x: at.x, y: at.y, opacity: 1)
496	        )
497	    }

519	
520	/// The model's one font string ↔ the panel's family + style pair.
521	///
522	/// Everything here tolerates a name this machine has no font for: a project
523	/// carries PostScript names, and the Text tab still has to open (and still has
524	/// to be able to change the face) on a machine missing that family.
525	enum TextFace {
526	    /// Installed families, sorted. Read once — `availableFontFamilies` walks
527	    /// the font registry, and this popup is rebuilt on every selection change.
528	    static let families: [String] = NSFontManager.shared.availableFontFamilies.sorted()
529	
530	    /// One member of a family: its PostScript name and the style label.
531	    struct Member {
532	        let name: String
533	        let style: String
534	    }
535	
536	    static func members(of family: String) -> [Member] {
537	        let raw = NSFontManager.shared.availableMembers(ofFontFamily: family) ?? []
538	        return raw.compactMap { entry in
539	            guard entry.count >= 2, let name = entry[0] as? String,
540	                  let style = entry[1] as? String
541	            else { return nil }
542	            return Member(name: name, style: style)
543	        }
544	    }
545	
546	    /// The family a stored PostScript name belongs to; the first installed
547	    /// family when the font is missing, so the popup always has a row.
548	    static func family(of postScriptName: String) -> String {
549	        if let font = NSFont(name: postScriptName, size: 12), let family = font.familyName {
550	            return family
551	        }
552	        return families.first ?? "Helvetica"
553	    }
554	
555	    /// The style label of a stored name ("SemiBold"), or "Regular".
556	    static func style(of postScriptName: String) -> String {
557	        let family = family(of: postScriptName)
558	        return members(of: family).first { $0.name == postScriptName }?.style ?? "Regular"
559	    }
560	
561	    /// The PostScript name for a family plus a style label, keeping the style
562	    /// across a family change when the new family has one by that name.
563	    static func postScriptName(family: String, style: String) -> String {
564	        let list = members(of: family)
565	        if let match = list.first(where: { $0.style == style }) { return match.name }
566	        if let regular = list.first(where: { $0.style == "Regular" }) { return regular.name }
567	        return list.first?.name ?? family
568	    }
569	}

161	    /// The gradient fill (§5.2's `shape.gradient`, format version 6): a
162	    /// geometry, an angle and the stops, all of it one `set_shape` patch.
163	    ///
164	    /// Three rules out of the schema show up here as UI, and none of them is
165	    /// this file's invention:
166	    ///
167	    ///  - **Every write sends the WHOLE object.** The core MERGES a nested
168	    ///    object into a stored one key by key (§5.2), but a stored `null` is
169	    ///    not an object: `actions::merge` replaces it with what the patch
170	    ///    carries, and the keys left out then come from `Gradient::default()`
171	    ///    rather than from what the clip had. This section is where a
172	    ///    gradient is turned ON from null, so it sends every key and is right
173	    ///    in both cases. `shadow` has carried that since M3 and `obscure`
174	    ///    since phase 3; `edited` below is where `gradient` joins them.
175	    ///  - **The Fill rows above stay live.** A gradient takes precedence over
176	    ///    `fill` and does not clear it, which is what makes this section's
177	    ///    Reset — one `{gradient: null}` — an exact inverse rather than a
178	    ///    shape that goes invisible. Disabling the colour underneath would
179	    ///    hide the value the Reset is about to bring back, so the note says
180	    ///    where the fill went instead of the panel pretending it is gone.
181	    ///  - **`line` and `arrow` get the rows DISABLED, not hidden.** The field
182	    ///    is stored and range-checked on every kind and read by the two area
183	    ///    kinds alone — `radius`'s precedent exactly — so flipping the Kind
184	    ///    popup to Line and back may not lose the ramp.
185	    func gradientSection() -> InspectorSection {
186	        let binding = self.binding
187	        let kinds = GradientKind.allCases
188	        func current() -> Gradient? { binding.shapeProps.gradient }
189	        func on() -> Bool { current() != nil }
190	        /// Whether this kind has an interior to fill at all.
191	        func area() -> Bool { !binding.shapeProps.kind.isLinear }
192	        func list() -> [GradientStop] { current()?.stops ?? [] }
193	        func at(_ index: Int) -> GradientStop? {
194	            let stops = list()
195	            return stops.indices.contains(index) ? stops[index] : nil
196	        }
197	        func ops(_ next: Gradient?) -> [ReelOp] {
198	            binding.ops(shape: ShapePatch(gradient: .some(next)))
199	        }
200	        /// The gradient with `change` applied and the other keys as they
201	        /// stand. This is the "send it whole" rule above, spelled once so that
202	        /// no row has to remember it.
203	        func edited(_ change: (inout Gradient) -> Void) -> [ReelOp] {
204	            guard var gradient = current() else { return [] }
205	            change(&gradient)
206	            return ops(gradient)
207	        }
208	        func edited(replacing index: Int, _ stop: GradientStop) -> [ReelOp] {
209	            var next = list()
210	            guard next.indices.contains(index) else { return [] }
211	            next[index] = stop
212	            return edited { $0.stops = next }
213	        }
214	        /// The mixed badge for one stop's field: a selection where some clip
215	        /// has no gradient, or none at that index, disagrees — which the
216	        /// `nil` says, the way `obscureSection`'s `mixedAt` says it.
217	        func mixedAt<T: Equatable>(_ index: Int, _ read: @escaping (GradientStop) -> T) -> Bool {
218	            binding.mixedShape { props -> T? in
219	                guard let stops = props.gradient?.stops, stops.indices.contains(index)
220	                else { return nil }
221	                return read(stops[index])
222	            }
223	        }
224	        /// The colour half way between two stops, component by component —
225	        /// which is exactly what `CGGradient` does between them, in the same
226	        /// sRGB space, so a handle added here sits ON the ramp rather than
227	        /// beside it. A three-component colour is an opaque one (`RGBA`'s own
228	        /// rule), so both are padded the same way before they are mixed.
229	        func midpoint(_ a: RGBA, _ b: RGBA) -> RGBA {
230	            func component(_ color: RGBA, _ index: Int) -> Double {
231	                index < color.count ? color[index] : (index == 3 ? 1 : 0)
232	            }
233	            return (0..<4).map { (component(a, $0) + component(b, $0)) / 2 }
234	        }
235	        /// A stop dropped into the WIDEST gap and coloured by the ramp that
236	        /// is already there, so Add changes the picture not at all: it puts a
237	        /// handle where the ramp already runs, which is what Add means in
238	        /// every gradient editor. The model cannot do this for you —
239	        /// `GradientStop`'s own default is black at 0, because serde has to
240	        /// fill a missing key without knowing which row was clicked.
241	        ///
242	        /// It inserts into the list as it is HELD, never into the sorted one.
243	        /// The rows are drawn in held order and the core deliberately does
244	        /// not police that order (`props_check.rs` argues the missing check
245	        /// where it would have gone), so sorting here would make every row
246	        /// jump the first time somebody pressed Add.
247	        func added(_ stops: [GradientStop]) -> [GradientStop] {
248	            guard stops.count >= 2 else { return Gradient.defaultStops }
249	            let ramp = stops.enumerated().sorted {
250	                $0.element.at == $1.element.at
251	                    ? $0.offset < $1.offset : $0.element.at < $1.element.at
252	            }
253	            var widest = -1.0
254	            var left = ramp[0]
255	            var right = ramp[1]
256	            for (a, b) in zip(ramp, ramp.dropFirst()) where b.element.at - a.element.at > widest {
257	                widest = b.element.at - a.element.at
258	                left = a
259	                right = b
260	            }
261	            var next = stops
262	            next.insert(
263	                GradientStop(
264	                    at: (left.element.at + right.element.at) / 2,
265	                    color: midpoint(left.element.color, right.element.color)),
266	                at: left.offset + 1)
267	            return next
268	        }
269	
270	        var rows: [NSView] = [
271	            inspectorCheckRow(
272	                "Gradient", binding, name: "Gradient", read: on,
273	                ops: { value in ops(value ? Gradient() : nil) },
274	                mixed: { binding.mixedShape { $0.gradient != nil } },
275	                enabled: area),
276	            inspectorPopupRow(
277	                "Kind", binding, name: "Gradient Kind", items: kinds.map { $0.displayName },
278	                read: { kinds.firstIndex(of: current()?.kind ?? .linear) ?? 0 },
279	                ops: { index in
280	                    guard kinds.indices.contains(index) else { return [] }
281	                    return edited { $0.kind = kinds[index] }
282	                },
283	                mixed: { binding.mixedShape { $0.gradient?.kind } },
284	                enabled: { on() && area() }),
285	            // Degrees from the RIGHT, counter-clockwise, and the same eight
286	            // quick picks the shadow's angle gets, because it is the same
287	            // convention and the crate has only the one.
288	            inspectorValueRow(
289	                "Angle", binding, name: "Gradient Angle", unit: "°", decimals: 0, min: 0,
290	                max: 360, quick: [0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 225, 270, 315],
291	                read: { current()?.angle ?? 0 },
292	                ops: { v in edited { $0.angle = v } },
293	                mixed: { binding.mixedShape { $0.gradient?.angle } },
294	                // A radial gradient has no direction to point: the model
295	                // stores the angle through the flip all the same, so coming
296	                // back to Linear finds the number where it was left.
297	                enabled: { on() && area() && current()?.kind == .linear }),
298	        ]
299	        for index in 0..<list().count {
300	            let swatch = OptionSwatchControl(
301	                read: { at(index)?.color.nsColor ?? .black },
302	                write: { color in
303	                    guard let stop = at(index),
304	                        let next = changedRGBA(color, from: stop.color)
305	                    else { return }
306	                    binding.apply(
307	                        "Gradient Stop",
308	                        edited(replacing: index, GradientStop(at: stop.at, color: next)))
309	                },
310	                enabled: area, onEdit: {})
311	            // A stop's position is 0–1 in the model and a PERCENTAGE here,
312	            // for `video.opacity`'s reason: the ramp is a distance across the
313	            // box, and nobody reads 0.35 of a box as a third of the way.
314	            let position = OptionFieldControl(
315	                width: InspectorMetrics.fieldWidth, unit: "%", decimals: 0, min: 0, max: 100,
316	                quick: [0, 25, 50, 75, 100],
317	                read: { (at(index)?.at ?? 0) * 100 },
318	                write: { value in
319	                    guard let stop = at(index) else { return }
320	                    binding.apply(
321	                        "Gradient Stop",
322	                        edited(replacing: index, GradientStop(at: value / 100, color: stop.color)))
323	                },
324	                enabled: area,
325	                onEdit: { binding.edited() })
326	            let remove = OptionButtonControl(
327	                title: "Remove",
328	                action: {
329	                    var next = list()
330	                    guard next.count > 2, next.indices.contains(index) else {
331	                        NSSound.beep()
332	                        return
333	                    }
334	                    next.remove(at: index)
335	                    binding.apply("Remove Stop", edited { $0.stops = next })
336	                },
337	                enabled: { area() && list().count > 2 }, onEdit: {})
338	            remove.toolTip =
339	                "Take this colour off the ramp — two stops is the floor, because one "
340	                + "colour is a fill and Fill above already spells that"
341	            rows.append(
342	                inspectorRow(
343	                    "Stop \(index + 1)", [swatch, position, remove],
344	                    mixed: { mixedAt(index) { $0.color } || mixedAt(index) { $0.at } }))
345	        }
346	        if !on() {
347	            rows.append(inspectorRow(nil, [InspectorRowLabel("No gradient.")]))
348	        }
349	        let add = OptionButtonControl(
350	            title: "Add Stop",
351	            action: {
352	                let next = added(list())
353	                guard next.count > list().count else {
354	                    NSSound.beep()
355	                    return
356	                }
357	                binding.apply("Add Stop", edited { $0.stops = next })
358	            },
359	            enabled: { area() && on() && list().count < Gradient.maxStops }, onEdit: {})
360	        add.toolTip =
361	            "Put a handle on the ramp where the ramp already is — the widest gap, "
362	            + "at the colour that is already there"
363	        rows.append(inspectorButtonRow([add, InspectorRowLabel("\(Gradient.maxStops) at most")]))
364	
365	        return InspectorSection(
366	            id: "shape.gradient", title: "Gradient",
367	            summary: {
368	                guard let gradient = current() else { return "off" }
369	                return "\(gradient.kind.displayName.lowercased()), \(gradient.stops.count) stops"
370	            },
371	            note: {
372	                guard area() else {
373	                    return "Fills the rectangle or ellipse; a line or arrow keeps its "
374	                        + "stroke colour."
375	                }
376	                guard on(), binding.shapeProps.fill != nil else { return nil }
377	                return "The gradient covers the Fill colour above; Reset brings it back."
378	            },
379	            reset: { binding.apply("Gradient", shape: ShapePatch(gradient: .some(nil))) },
380	            defaultExpanded: false,

1	// app/Sources/GraphicPane.swift — the Clip tab's GRAPHIC sections (road map
2	// 10 §5j, G5a): Source (in `GraphicPane+Source.swift`), Properties from the
3	// module's schema (rows from `GraphicSchemaRows.swift`), Size and Timeline.
4	// With no action selected every write is `set_graphic`. With one selected, a
5	// Properties write — Reset's included — goes to the action's END with the
6	// module's current schema, one `set_action_end` naming `graphic.props.<key>`,
7	// except an `animate: false` prop's, which stays the clip's (spec §11 G-34
8	// (l), G-41 (d), G-42 (d)); Size and
9	// Timeline still write `set_graphic`, so their rows are ⊘. The core
10	// validates both.
11	//
12	// **Never shown itself**: like `ShapePane`, a factory `ClipPane` holds and
13	// calls when EVERY selected clip is a graphic clip.
14	//
15	// **Several graphic clips.** Source and Size always; Properties only when
16	// every clip is drawn by ONE module (one schema to build rows from, and the
17	// schema `set_graphic` needs), and Timeline only for one clip — its `in`
18	// and `length` are that clip's own. With different modules Source says so
19	// and names them (spec §11 G-15).
20	//
21	// **The schema is the registry's** (`GraphicRegistry.entry(named:for:)`,
22	// main only), the same read `AgentServer+Graphics.compiledModule` makes for
23	// the tool path. Nothing here rescans the store from an observer: `drain()`
24	// is not re-entrant (road map 10 §10.6 G3a).

38	final class GraphicPane: InspectorPaneView {
39	    /// The report of each module/revision/library/frame hash/size seen, and
40	    /// the last report per clip — what a miss answers while a live gesture
41	    /// runs, so the signature holds still through a drag.
42	    var reportMemo: [String: GraphicClipReport] = [:]
43	    var lastReports: [UInt32: GraphicClipReport] = [:]
44	    /// The parsed schema of the last module asked, keyed "name|revision".
45	    var schemaMemo: (key: String, schema: GraphicSchema)?
46	    /// Each clip's recipe layer source under `layerProject`, the handle it
47	    /// was read from; emptied when the binding's project is another handle.
48	    weak var layerProject: ReelProject?
49	    var layerMemo: [UInt32: RecipeSourceRef] = [:]
50	
51	    /// Whether the graphic sections apply: they write `set_graphic`, which
52	    /// errors on any other kind, so a mixed selection gets none of them.
53	    var allGraphic: Bool {
54	        !binding.clips.isEmpty && binding.graphicClips.count == binding.clips.count
55	    }
56	
57	    /// The one module every selected graphic clip is drawn by.
58	    struct Shared {
59	        let name: String
60	        let file: GraphicModuleFile?
61	        let entry: GraphicRegistry.Entry?
62	    }
63	
64	    /// nil when the selection's modules differ (or it holds no graphic).
65	    func shared() -> Shared? {
66	        let names = Set(binding.graphicClips.compactMap { $0.graphic?.name })
67	        guard names.count == 1, let name = names.first else { return nil }
68	        let document = binding.document
69	        return Shared(
70	            name: name, file: document?.graphicStore?.module(named: name),
71	            entry: document.flatMap {
72	                GraphicRegistry.shared.entry(named: name, for: $0.recipeKey)
73	            })
74	    }
75	
76	    /// The compiled schema of `shared`, parsed in the module's order, and
77	    /// the registry's dictionary the ops carry. Parsed once per name and
78	    /// revision (`schemaMemo`).
79	    func schema(_ shared: Shared?) -> (schema: GraphicSchema, raw: [String: Any])? {
80	        guard let shared, case .compiled(let module, let revision, _, let raw)? = shared.entry
81	        else { return nil }
82	        let key = "\(shared.name)|\(revision)"
83	        if let memo = schemaMemo, memo.key == key { return (memo.schema, raw) }
84	        let parsed = GraphicSchema(describeJSON: module.describeJSON(), schema: raw)
85	        schemaMemo = (key, parsed)
86	        return (parsed, raw)
87	    }

89	    /// The selection's stored props, merged; the first clip holding a key wins.
90	    func storedProps() -> [String: GraphicPropValue] {
91	        var merged: [String: GraphicPropValue] = [:]
92	        for clip in binding.graphicClips {
93	            merged.merge(clip.graphic?.props ?? [:]) { first, _ in first }
94	        }
95	        return merged
96	    }
97	
98	    /// The selected action's end props (G-34 (a)); none with no action
99	    /// selected. Its keys the schema lacks are the action's stale rows.
100	    func endProps() -> [String: GraphicPropValue] {
101	        binding.selectedAction?.end.graphic?.props ?? [:]
102	    }
103	
104	    /// The asset folder's file names, sorted.
105	    func assetNames() -> [String] {
106	        (binding.document?.graphicStore?.scan.assets.map(\.name) ?? []).sorted()
107	    }
108	
109	    /// What the graphics folder's scan skipped or could not watch, in its own
110	    /// sentences — the Source section's folder rows (G-24 (b)).
111	    func folderWarnings() -> [String] {
112	        binding.document?.graphicStore?.scan.warnings ?? []
113	    }
114	
115	    /// The schema's entries whole (a default, bounds or options a row is
116	    /// built from), the stale keys (the clip's, then the selected action's
117	    /// end's, `actionStaleKeys`, a declared key no action may animate
118	    /// included, G-41), each asset popup's names (the selected end's
119	    /// included, G-42), the
120	    /// diagnostics' messages and the folder's warnings. Stored values, the
121	    /// revision and the playhead are NOT here: they are read fresh by
122	    /// `refresh()`.
123	    override var structureSignature: String {
124	        guard allGraphic else { return super.structureSignature + "|-" }
125	        let shared = self.shared()
126	        let parsed = schema(shared)
127	        let keys = parsed?.schema.entries.map { String(describing: $0) } ?? []
128	        let stale = GraphicSchemaRows.staleKeys(stored: storedProps(), schema: parsed?.schema)
129	        var messages = ["-", "-"]
130	        if let shared, let clip = binding.graphicClips.first, let document = binding.document {
131	            let version = GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)?.libraryVersion
132	            let report = self.report(for: clip, shared, libraryVersion: version ?? "")
133	            func spell(_ list: [GraphicDiagnostic]) -> String {
134	                list.map { "\($0.level):\($0.line ?? -1):\($0.column ?? -1):\($0.message)" }
135	                    .joined(separator: "¶")
136	            }
137	            messages = [spell(report.compile), spell(report.render)]
138	        }
139	        messages.append(folderWarnings().joined(separator: "¶"))
140	        return [
141	            super.structureSignature, shared?.name ?? "mixed", keys.joined(separator: ","),
142	            stale.joined(separator: ","), assetSignature(parsed?.schema),
143	            GraphicSchemaRows.actionStaleKeys(end: endProps(), schema: parsed?.schema)
144	                .joined(separator: ","),
145	        ].joined(separator: "|") + "|" + messages.joined(separator: "|")
146	    }
147	
148	    /// Each asset entry's popup names, from the rows' own
149	    /// `GraphicSchemaRows.assetNames` call, the selected action's end's names
150	    /// counting (G-42 (d)): names joined by ",", entries by ";".
151	    private func assetSignature(_ schema: GraphicSchema?) -> String {
152	        let files = assetNames(), clips = binding.graphicClips
153	        return (schema?.entries ?? []).filter { $0.type == "asset" }.map {
154	            GraphicSchemaRows.assetNames(for: $0, files: files, clips: clips, end: endProps())
155	                .joined(separator: ",")
156	        }.joined(separator: ";")
157	    }

161	    /// One row per schema key in the module's order, then the stale keys,
162	    /// sorted, then — with an action selected — the end's own stale keys
163	    /// (G-34 (l), O2), a declared key whose entry is not `animatable` among
164	    /// them (G-41 (c)). With no compiled schema every stored key is stale.
165	    /// Reset nulls every stored key; with an action selected it writes each
166	    /// declared default through the rows' own split, into the END (an
167	    /// asset's `null` as `""`, G-42 (d)), an `animate: false` prop's (G-41
168	    /// (d)) onto the clip (O7). Its `differs` folds from the rows.
169	    func propertiesSection() -> InspectorSection {
170	        let binding = self.binding
171	        let shared = self.shared()
172	        let parsed = schema(shared)
173	        let clips = { binding.graphicClips }
174	        let assets = { [weak self] in self?.assetNames() ?? [] }
175	        var rows: [NSView] = parsed?.schema.entries.map {
176	            GraphicSchemaRows.row(
177	                $0, binding, clips: clips, schema: parsed?.raw ?? [:], assets: assets)
178	        } ?? []
179	        let stored = storedProps()
180	        for key in GraphicSchemaRows.staleKeys(stored: stored, schema: parsed?.schema) {
181	            rows.append(
182	                GraphicSchemaRows.staleRow(
183	                    key: key, value: stored[key] ?? .null, binding, clips: clips))
184	        }
185	        let ends = endProps()
186	        let declared = Set(parsed?.schema.keys ?? [])
187	        for key in GraphicSchemaRows.actionStaleKeys(end: ends, schema: parsed?.schema) {
188	            rows.append(
189	                GraphicSchemaRows.actionStaleRow(
190	                    key: key, value: ends[key] ?? .null, declared: declared.contains(key), binding))
191	        }
192	        let note: String?
193	        if parsed == nil {
194	            note = "The module did not compile — see Source. Stored values are listed below."
195	        } else if parsed?.schema.entries.isEmpty == true {
196	            note = "The module declares no properties."
197	        } else {
198	            note = nil
199	        }
200	        let count = parsed?.schema.entries.count ?? 0
201	        return InspectorSection(
202	            id: "graphic.properties", title: "Properties",
203	            summary: { count == 1 ? "1 property" : "\(count) properties" },
204	            note: note.map { text -> () -> String? in { text } },
205	            reset: {
206	                if binding.selectedAction != nil {
207	                    let entries = parsed?.schema.entries ?? []
208	                    let defaults = Dictionary(
209	                        entries.map { ($0.key, $0.default) }, uniquingKeysWith: { first, _ in first })
210	                    binding.apply(
211	                        "Reset Graphic Properties",
212	                        binding.ops(
213	                            graphic: defaults, entries: entries, clips: clips(), schema: parsed?.raw))
214	                    return
215	                }
216	                let targets = clips()
217	                var keys = Set<String>()
218	                for clip in targets { keys.formUnion(clip.graphic?.props.keys.map { $0 } ?? []) }
219	                guard !keys.isEmpty else { return NSSound.beep() }
220	                binding.apply(
221	                    "Reset Graphic Properties",
222	                    [GraphicSchemaRows.op(
223	                        clips: targets,
224	                        props: Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: keys.map { ($0, NSNull()) }),
225	                        schema: parsed?.raw)])
226	            },
227	            defaultExpanded: true,
228	            rows: rows)
229	    }

313	                }]),

1	// app/Sources/GraphicPane+Source.swift — the Graphic sub-tab's Source
2	// section (road map 10 §5j, G5a): which module draws the clip, the three
3	// buttons (Open in Editor, Reveal in Finder, Duplicate as New Graphic…), and
4	// what the module says about the clip, each group under its own heading
5	// (#221): "Compiling the module" over its compile (an error, or what its top
6	// level warned), when there is any; the clip's FIRST frame drawn and
7	// rasterized at the clip's own size, when one was drawn, so a missing font
8	// or a size mismatch shows here (G3c's owed warning, road map 10 §10.6); and
9	// "In the graphics folder" over what the folder's scan skipped or could not
10	// watch, each with Reveal (G-24 (b)).
11	//
12	// **The report is the paused frame's own two calls** — `module.svg` then
13	// `library.rasterize` at `graphic.width × height`
14	// (`LayerRenderersGraphic.swift`) — memoised by module, revision, library,
15	// the recipe's frame hash and the size, so a miss costs one paused frame.
16	// While a live gesture runs nothing is recomputed: a miss answers the
17	// clip's last report.
18	
19	import AppKit
20	
21	/// What a graphic clip's module says about it: its compile's diagnostics,
22	/// and the first frame's — drawn at the graphic's `frame`.
23	struct GraphicClipReport: Equatable {
24	    let compile: [GraphicDiagnostic]
25	    let render: [GraphicDiagnostic]
26	    let frame: Int?
27	
28	    static let empty = GraphicClipReport(compile: [], render: [], frame: nil)
29	}
30	
31	extension GraphicPane {
32	    /// The module, its file and revision, the three buttons and the
33	    /// diagnostics. With clips of different modules, a note naming them.
34	    func sourceSection() -> InspectorSection {
35	        guard let first = shared() else {
36	            let names = Set(binding.graphicClips.compactMap { $0.graphic?.name }).sorted()
37	            let listed = names.joined(separator: ", ")
38	            return InspectorSection(
39	                id: "graphic.source", title: "Source", summary: { "\(names.count) modules" },
40	                defaultExpanded: false,
41	                rows: [
42	                    InspectorNoteLabel { "Drawn by different modules: \(listed)" },
43	                    InspectorNoteLabel { "Select one module's clips to edit its properties." },
44	                ])
45	        }
46	        let current = { [weak self] in self?.shared() }
47	        func metaName() -> String {
48	            if case .compiled(_, _, let meta, _)? = current()?.entry,
49	               let name = meta["name"] as? String, !name.isEmpty
50	            {
51	                return name
52	            }
53	            return current()?.name ?? first.name
54	        }
55	        func revision() -> String {
56	            guard let file = current()?.file else { return "missing" }
57	            return String(file.revision.prefix(8))
58	        }
59	        let open: () -> Void = { [weak self] in self?.openFile() }
60	        let hasFile = { current()?.file != nil }
61	        let duplicate = OptionButtonControl(
62	            title: "Duplicate as New Graphic…",
63	            action: { [weak self] in
64	                guard let self, let shared = current(), let file = shared.file else {
65	                    return NSSound.beep()
66	                }
67	                self.duplicateAsNewGraphic(file, schema: self.schema(shared)?.raw)
68	            },
69	            enabled: hasFile, onEdit: {})
70	        var rows: [NSView] = [
71	            inspectorRow("Name", [inspectorReadout(width: 170) { metaName() }]),
72	            inspectorRow("File", [inspectorReadout(width: 170) { "\(first.name).js" }]),
73	            inspectorRow("Revision", [inspectorReadout(width: 170) { revision() }]),
74	            inspectorButtonRow([
75	                OptionButtonControl(
76	                    title: "Open in Editor", action: open, enabled: hasFile, onEdit: {}),
77	                OptionButtonControl(
78	                    title: "Reveal in Finder",
79	                    action: {
80	                        guard let url = current()?.file?.url else { return NSSound.beep() }
81	                        NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([url])
82	                    },
83	                    enabled: hasFile, onEdit: {}),
84	            ]),
85	            inspectorButtonRow([duplicate]),
86	        ]
87	        var report = GraphicClipReport.empty
88	        if let clip = binding.graphicClips.first, let document = binding.document {
89	            let version = GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)?.libraryVersion
90	            report = self.report(for: clip, first, libraryVersion: version ?? "")
91	        }
92	        let diagnostics = report.compile + report.render
93	        if !report.compile.isEmpty {
94	            rows.append(InspectorNoteLabel { "Compiling the module" })
95	            rows += report.compile.map { GraphicDiagnosticRow($0, onOpen: open) }
96	        }
97	        if report.frame != nil {
98	            let checked = report.render.isEmpty
99	                ? "No errors or warnings at the clip's first frame"
100	                : "Checked at the clip's first frame"
101	            rows.append(InspectorNoteLabel { checked })
102	            rows += report.render.map { GraphicDiagnosticRow($0, onOpen: open) }
103	        }
104	        let folder = folderWarnings()
105	        if !folder.isEmpty {
106	            let reveal: () -> Void = { [weak self] in
107	                guard let url = self?.binding.document?.graphicStore?.folderURL,
108	                      FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url.path)
109	                else { return NSSound.beep() }
110	                NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([url])
111	            }
112	            rows.append(InspectorNoteLabel { "In the graphics folder" })
113	            rows += folder.map {
114	                GraphicDiagnosticRow(
115	                    GraphicDiagnostic(
116	                        level: "warning", message: $0, line: nil, column: nil, frame: nil),
117	                    openTitle: "Reveal", help: "Reveal the graphics folder in Finder",
118	                    onOpen: reveal)
119	            }
120	        }
121	        let errors = diagnostics.filter { $0.level == "error" }.count
122	        let warnings = diagnostics.count - errors + folder.count
123	        return InspectorSection(
124	            id: "graphic.source", title: "Source",
125	            summary: {
126	                errors > 0 ? (errors == 1 ? "1 error" : "\(errors) errors")
127	                    : warnings > 0 ? (warnings == 1 ? "1 warning" : "\(warnings) warnings")
128	                    : metaName()
129	            },
130	            defaultExpanded: false,
131	            rows: rows)
132	    }
133	
134	    /// Opens the shared module's file in the app the system gives `.js`.
135	    func openFile() {
136	        guard let url = shared()?.file?.url else { return NSSound.beep() }
137	        NSWorkspace.shared.open(url)
138	    }
139	
140	    /// The module's compile, and `clip`'s first frame drawn and rasterized at
141	    /// the clip's own size — through the memo, and never recomputed while a
142	    /// live gesture runs.
143	    func report(
144	        for clip: ClipSnapshot, _ shared: Shared, libraryVersion: String
145	    ) -> GraphicClipReport {
146	        let module: GraphicModule, revision: String
147	        switch shared.entry {
148	        case nil:
149	            return GraphicClipReport(
150	                compile: [GraphicDiagnostic.noModule(shared.name)],
151	                render: [], frame: nil)
152	        case .failed(let diagnostics, _)?:
153	            return GraphicClipReport(compile: diagnostics, render: [], frame: nil)
154	        case .compiled(let compiled, let hash, _, _)?:
155	            module = compiled
156	            revision = hash
157	        }
158	        guard let graphic = clip.graphic, let document = binding.document else { return .empty }
159	        if document.isLiveEditing { return lastReports[clip.id] ?? .empty }
160	        guard let set = GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey),
161	              let source = layerSource(of: clip),
162	              case .graphic(_, let hash, let frame, let propsJSON, let ctxJSON) = source
163	        else { return .empty }
164	        let key = [
165	            shared.name, revision, libraryVersion, hash, "\(graphic.width)×\(graphic.height)",
166	        ].joined(separator: "|")
167	        if let hit = reportMemo[key] {
168	            lastReports[clip.id] = hit
169	            return hit
170	        }
171	        var render: [GraphicDiagnostic] = []
172	        do {
173	            let drawn = try module.svg(
174	                frame: frame, propsJSON: propsJSON, ctxJSON: ctxJSON,
175	                budgetMs: GraphicRegistry.previewBudgetMs)
176	            render += drawn.warnings
177	            do {
178	                let raster = try set.library.rasterize(
179	                    drawn.svg, width: graphic.width, height: graphic.height)
180	                render += raster.warnings
181	            } catch {
182	                render += GraphicDiagnostic.of(error)
183	            }
184	        } catch {
185	            render += GraphicDiagnostic.of(error)
186	        }
187	        let report = GraphicClipReport(
188	            compile: module.compileWarnings, render: render, frame: frame)
189	        if reportMemo.count >= 64 { reportMemo.removeAll() }
190	        reportMemo[key] = report
191	        lastReports[clip.id] = report
192	        return report
193	    }
194	
195	    /// `clip`'s layer source in the recipe at its start, through
196	    /// `layerMemo`: `recipe(at:)` is asked only on a miss, and the memo is
197	    /// emptied when the binding's project is another handle.
198	    func layerSource(of clip: ClipSnapshot) -> RecipeSourceRef? {
199	        guard let project = binding.project else { return nil }
200	        if project !== layerProject {
201	            layerMemo = [:]
202	            layerProject = project
203	        }
204	        if let hit = layerMemo[clip.id] { return hit }
205	        guard let layer = project.recipe(at: clip.start)?.layers
206	            .first(where: { $0.clip == clip.id })
207	        else { return nil }
208	        layerMemo[clip.id] = layer.source
209	        return layer.source
210	    }
211	
212	    /// Copies the module's file under a new name the person types, then
213	    /// repoints the selected clips at it with `set_graphic {name}` — the
214	    /// copy is not undoable (G-3), the repoint is one step. The MCP mirror is
215	    /// `write_graphic` of the source under the new name, then `set_graphic`.
216	    func duplicateAsNewGraphic(_ file: GraphicModuleFile, schema: [String: Any]?) {
217	        guard let store = binding.document?.graphicStore else { return NSSound.beep() }
218	        let suggestion = store.uniqueModuleName(file.name + "-copy")
219	        let alert = NSAlert()
220	        alert.alertStyle = .informational
221	        alert.messageText = "Duplicate \(file.name).js as a new graphic"
222	        alert.informativeText =
223	            "The copy is written into the package's graphics/ folder and the selected clips "
224	            + "are drawn by it. Writing the file cannot be undone; switching the clips can."
225	        let field = NSTextField(string: suggestion)
226	        field.frame = NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 240, height: 24)
227	        field.placeholderString = "Module name"
228	        alert.accessoryView = field
229	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Duplicate")
230	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Cancel")
231	        alert.window.initialFirstResponder = field
232	        guard alert.runModal() == .alertFirstButtonReturn else { return }
233	        let name = field.stringValue.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
234	        func refuse(_ sentence: String) {
235	            NSAlert(error: NSError(
236	                domain: "FrameJob", code: 1, userInfo: [NSLocalizedDescriptionKey: sentence]))
237	                .runModal()
238	        }
239	        guard GraphicStore.isModuleName(name) else { return refuse(GraphicStore.nameSentence(name)) }
240	        guard !store.holdsModule(named: name) else {
241	            return refuse("graphics/\(name).js already exists")
242	        }
243	        do {
244	            try store.write(name: name, source: String(decoding: file.bytes, as: UTF8.self))
245	        } catch {
246	            return refuse("graphics/\(name).js could not be written: \(error.localizedDescription)")
247	        }
248	        store.rescan()
249	        let clips = binding.graphicClips.map(\.id)
250	        binding.apply(
251	            "Duplicate Graphic",
252	            clips.isEmpty ? [] : [.setGraphicRaw(clips: clips, patch: ["name": name], schema: schema)])
253	    }
254	}
255	
256	/// One diagnostic: "line L, column C — message", an error in the strong
257	/// ink and a warning in the muted one. A click on it, or on its Open, opens
258	/// the module in the editor; a folder row's button is Reveal instead.
259	final class GraphicDiagnosticRow: NSView {
260	    let diagnostic: GraphicDiagnostic
261	    private let onOpen: () -> Void
262	    let label = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "")
263	
264	    init(
265	        _ d: GraphicDiagnostic, openTitle: String = "Open",
266	        help: String = "Open the module in the editor", onOpen: @escaping () -> Void
267	    ) {
268	        diagnostic = d
269	        self.onOpen = onOpen
270	        super.init(frame: .zero)
271	        var place = ""
272	        if let line = d.line {
273	            place = d.column.map { "line \(line), column \($0) — " } ?? "line \(line) — "
274	        }
275	        label.stringValue = place + d.message
276	        label.font = DS.sans(11)
277	        label.textColor = d.level == "error" ? DS.textStrong : DS.textMuted
278	        label.isSelectable = false
279	        label.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = 200
280	        label.setContentCompressionResistancePriority(.defaultLow, for: .horizontal)
281	        let open = OptionButtonControl(
282	            title: openTitle, action: { [weak self] in self?.onOpen() }, enabled: { true },
283	            onEdit: {})
284	        open.setContentHuggingPriority(.required, for: .horizontal)
285	        let row = NSStackView(views: [label, open])
286	        row.orientation = .horizontal
287	        row.alignment = .top
288	        row.spacing = 6
289	        row.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
290	        addSubview(row)
291	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
292	            row.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: topAnchor),
293	            row.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bottomAnchor),
294	            row.leadingAnchor.constraint(
295	                equalTo: leadingAnchor, constant: InspectorMetrics.markGutter),
296	            row.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: trailingAnchor),
297	        ])
298	        toolTip = help
299	    }
300	
301	    @available(*, unavailable)
302	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
303	        fatalError("GraphicDiagnosticRow does not support NSCoder")
304	    }
305	
306	    override func mouseDown(with event: NSEvent) {
307	        onOpen()
308	    }
309	}

1	import AppKit
2	
3	/// The Clip tab's TEXT sections (spec §4.3): content, face, colour,
4	/// alignment, spacing, outline, backdrop, the box mode, how the words arrive
5	/// and leave, and the four presets.
6	///
7	/// **This pane is never shown**: since the six tabs became three it is a
8	/// factory `ClipPane` holds and calls, right after Transform, when EVERY
9	/// selected clip is a text clip. Shadow is not in the list any more — it is
10	/// one field (`video.shadow`) shared with the video and shape sections, so the
11	/// Clip tab carries it once, in the effects group.
12	///
13	/// The model stores ONE font string — a PostScript name (§5.2's
14	/// `"SourceSans3-SemiBold"`) — while the panel offers the two popups people
15	/// expect, family and style. `TextFace` is the whole translation between
16	/// them, and it is deliberately tolerant: a project made on another machine
17	/// can name a face this one does not have, and the pane must still open.
18	final class TextPane: InspectorPaneView {
19	    /// Whether the text sections apply: they write `set_text`, which errors on
20	    /// any other kind, so a mixed selection gets none of them.
21	    var allText: Bool {
22	        !binding.clips.isEmpty && binding.textClips.count == binding.clips.count
23	    }
24	
25	    /// A family change replaces the style popup's ITEMS, so it has to be part
26	    /// of the rebuild signature — refreshing alone would leave the old
27	    /// family's styles listed.
28	    override var structureSignature: String {
29	        super.structureSignature + "|" + TextFace.family(of: binding.textProps.font)
30	    }
31	
32	    // MARK: Content
33	
34	    /// The footnote on a word-styled page whose timings a content edit
35	    /// dropped (road map 8 §5e), and the Animation section's on a styled
36	    /// page, whose reveal the word style replaces (spec §11 W-5). The second
37	    /// is short on purpose: its row is 244 pt at the 280 pt narrowest
38	    /// inspector (`DocumentPane.transparencyNote` has the arithmetic, #70).
39	    static let untimedNote = "Not timed — regenerate to time it again"
40	    static let wordStyleNote = "Word style wins; the reveal does not apply."
41	
42	    func contentSection() -> InspectorSection {
43	        let binding = self.binding
44	        let area = InspectorTextArea(
45	            read: { binding.textProps.content },
46	            // Per clip: a timed page keeps its words while the count holds
47	            // and sends `words: []` beside the content when it does not.
48	            write: { value in binding.apply("Edit Text", binding.ops(textContent: value)) },
49	            enabled: { !binding.textClips.isEmpty },
50	            onEdit: { binding.edited() })
51	        return InspectorSection(
52	            id: "text.content", title: "Content",
53	            summary: {
54	                let line = binding.textProps.content
55	                    .split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).first.map(String.init) ?? ""
56	                return line.isEmpty ? "empty" : line
57	            },
58	            note: {
59	                binding.textProps.isUntimedPage ? Self.untimedNote : nil
60	            },
61	            rows: [inspectorRow(nil, [area], binding: binding,
62	                                writes: binding.ops(textContent: binding.textProps.content),
63	                                discrete: true)])
64	    }
65	
66	    // MARK: Face
67	
68	    func fontSection() -> InspectorSection {
69	        let binding = self.binding
70	        let families = TextFace.families
71	        let family = TextFace.family(of: binding.textProps.font)
72	        let members = TextFace.members(of: family)
73	        let font = binding.ops(text: TextPatch(font: binding.textProps.font))
74	
75	        let familyPopup = OptionPopupControl(
76	            width: 150, items: families,
77	            read: { families.firstIndex(of: TextFace.family(of: binding.textProps.font)) ?? 0 },
78	            write: { index in
79	                guard families.indices.contains(index) else { return }
80	                let current = binding.textProps.font
81	                let name = TextFace.postScriptName(
82	                    family: families[index], style: TextFace.style(of: current))
83	                binding.apply("Font", text: TextPatch(font: name))
84	            },
85	            enabled: { true },
86	            onEdit: { binding.edited() })
87	
88	        let stylePopup = OptionPopupControl(
89	            width: 116, items: members.map { $0.style },
90	            read: {
91	                let name = binding.textProps.font
92	                return members.firstIndex { $0.name == name } ?? 0
93	            },
94	            write: { index in
95	                guard members.indices.contains(index) else { return }
96	                binding.apply("Font", text: TextPatch(font: members[index].name))
97	            },
98	            enabled: { !members.isEmpty },
99	            onEdit: { binding.edited() })
100	
101	        return InspectorSection(
102	            id: "text.font", title: "Font",
103	            summary: { String(format: "%.0f px", binding.textProps.size) },
104	            defaultExpanded: false,
105	            rows: [
106	                inspectorRow(
107	                    "Family", [familyPopup], mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.font } },
108	                    binding: binding, writes: font),
109	                inspectorRow("Style", [stylePopup], binding: binding, writes: font),
110	                inspectorValueRow(
111	                    "Size", binding, name: "Font Size", unit: " px", decimals: 0, min: 6,
112	                    max: 800, quick: [24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 144], slider: false,
113	                    read: { binding.textProps.size },
114	                    ops: { binding.ops(text: TextPatch(size: $0)) },
115	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.size } }),
116	            ])
117	    }
118	
119	    // MARK: Style
120	
121	    func styleSection() -> InspectorSection {
122	        let binding = self.binding
123	        let aligns = ["left", "center", "right"]
124	        let valigns = ["top", "middle", "bottom"]
125	        let text = binding.textProps
126	        let align = OptionSegmentedControl(
127	            segments: [
128	                ("text.alignleft", "L", "Align left"),
129	                ("text.aligncenter", "C", "Align center"),
130	                ("text.alignright", "R", "Align right"),
131	            ],
132	            read: { aligns.firstIndex(of: binding.textProps.align) ?? 1 },
133	            write: { index in
134	                guard aligns.indices.contains(index) else { return }
135	                binding.apply("Alignment", text: TextPatch(align: aligns[index]))
136	            },
137	            segmentEnabled: nil, enabled: { true },
138	            onEdit: { binding.edited() })
139	        let valign = OptionSegmentedControl(
140	            segments: [
141	                ("align.vertical.top", "⤒", "Align to the top of the box"),
142	                ("align.vertical.center", "↕", "Center in the box"),
143	                ("align.vertical.bottom", "⤓", "Align to the bottom of the box"),
144	            ],
145	            read: { valigns.firstIndex(of: binding.textProps.valign) ?? 1 },
146	            write: { index in
147	                guard valigns.indices.contains(index) else { return }
148	                binding.apply("Alignment", text: TextPatch(valign: valigns[index]))
149	            },
150	            segmentEnabled: nil, enabled: { true },
151	            onEdit: { binding.edited() })
152	
153	        return InspectorSection(
154	            id: "text.style", title: "Style",
155	            summary: { binding.textProps.align },
156	            reset: {
157	                let defaults = TextProps()
158	                binding.apply(
159	                    "Text Style",
160	                    text: TextPatch(
161	                        color: defaults.color, align: defaults.align, valign: defaults.valign,
162	                        lineSpacing: defaults.lineSpacing, tracking: defaults.tracking,
163	                        textCase: defaults.textCase))
164	            },
165	            defaultExpanded: false,
166	            rows: [
167	                inspectorColorRow(
168	                    "Color", binding, name: "Text Color", read: { binding.textProps.color },
169	                    ops: { binding.ops(text: TextPatch(color: $0)) },
170	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.color } }),

341	    /// How the words arrive and how they leave (§4.3, format version 5).
342	    ///
343	    /// Three controls for three keys: which reveal, how long it takes to
344	    /// arrive, and how long it takes to leave. The core turns them into one
345	    /// number per frame — nothing here draws or times anything, and the
346	    /// section cannot show the reveal's progress, because the progress is a
347	    /// fact about the frame under the playhead and not about the clip.
348	    ///
349	    /// `animation` is a whole OBJECT in the patch, so every row re-sends all
350	    /// three keys. The core MERGES a nested object key by key (§5.2), but a
351	    /// stored `null` is not an object — turning the reveal ON replaces the
352	    /// null with what this patch carries, and a key left out would then come
353	    /// from the struct's default and silently reset what the user did not
354	    /// touch. A section that knows all three keys is right in both cases.
355	    /// Turning the popup to None sends an explicit null, which is the
356	    /// model's "no animation".
357	    ///
358	    /// One thing worth knowing before animating this section from an action:
359	    /// `in` and `out` are numbers, so an action END patch would interpolate
360	    /// them and slide the animation's own timebase mid-reveal. The kind is a
361	    /// string and switches at the end, which is the sane half.
362	    func animationSection() -> InspectorSection {
363	        let binding = self.binding
364	        let kinds = TextAnimationKind.allCases
365	        let items = ["None"] + kinds.map { $0.displayName }
366	        func current() -> TextAnimation { binding.textProps.animation ?? TextAnimation() }
367	        func on() -> Bool { binding.textProps.animation != nil }
368	        func free() -> Bool { binding.textProps.wordStyle == nil }
369	        func ops(_ next: TextAnimation) -> [ReelOp] {
370	            binding.ops(text: TextPatch(animation: .some(next)))
371	        }
372	        return InspectorSection(
373	            id: "text.animation", title: "Reveal",
374	            summary: {
375	                guard let animation = binding.textProps.animation else { return "off" }
376	                return animation.kind.displayName.lowercased()
377	                    + String(format: " · %.2f s", ReelTime.seconds(animation.inDuration))
378	            },
379	            note: { free() ? nil : Self.wordStyleNote },
380	            reset: { binding.apply("Animation", text: TextPatch(animation: .some(nil))) },
381	            defaultExpanded: false,
382	            rows: [
383	                inspectorPopupRow(
384	                    "Reveal", binding, name: "Text Animation", items: items,
385	                    read: {
386	                        guard let kind = binding.textProps.animation?.kind else { return 0 }
387	                        return (kinds.firstIndex(of: kind) ?? 0) + 1
388	                    },
389	                    ops: { index in
390	                        guard index > 0, kinds.indices.contains(index - 1) else {
391	                            return binding.ops(text: TextPatch(animation: .some(nil)))
392	                        }
393	                        // The durations as they stand: switching the reveal
394	                        // must not reset the timing the user chose for it.
395	                        var a = current()
396	                        a.kind = kinds[index - 1]
397	                        return ops(a)
398	                    },
399	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.animation?.kind } }, enabled: free),
400	                inspectorValueRow(
401	                    "In", binding, name: "Animation In", unit: " s", decimals: 2, min: 0, max: 10,
402	                    quick: [0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2],
403	                    read: { ReelTime.seconds(current().inDuration) },
404	                    ops: { value in
405	                        var a = current()
406	                        a.inDuration = binding.frameTicks(seconds: value)
407	                        return ops(a)
408	                    },
409	                    mixed: { binding.mixedText { $0.animation?.inDuration } },
410	                    enabled: { on() && free() }),
411	                inspectorValueRow(
412	                    "Out", binding, name: "Animation Out", unit: " s", decimals: 2, min: 0,
413	                    max: 10, quick: [0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2],
414	                    read: { ReelTime.seconds(current().outDuration) },
415	                    ops: { value in
416	                        var a = current()
417	                        a.outDuration = binding.frameTicks(seconds: value)
418	                        return ops(a)
419	                    },

459	/// One text preset (§4.3). Sizes and positions are FRACTIONS of the canvas so
460	/// a preset means the same thing on a 4K canvas as on a vertical one: a size
461	/// of the canvas's SHORT side, a position of its width and height (spec §11
462	/// VR-41), so a tall canvas gets the line height a wide one has.
463	struct TextPreset {
464	    let name: String
465	    let font: String
466	    let sizeFraction: Double
467	    let xFraction: Double
468	    let yFraction: Double
469	    let align: String
470	    let backdrop: BackdropProps?
471	    /// Of H, on a canvas taller than wide, in place of `yFraction` (the Caption
472	    /// row's 0.25, VR-41); nil keeps `yFraction` on every canvas.
473	    var tallYFraction: Double? = nil
474	
475	    /// The font size on `canvas`: `sizeFraction` of `min(W, H)`. On a canvas at
476	    /// least as wide as tall that is H, so the old `H × sizeFraction` is kept to the bit.
477	    func size(on canvas: CGSize) -> Double {
478	        (sizeFraction * Double(min(canvas.width, canvas.height))).rounded()
479	    }
480	
481	    /// Where the box's centre sits on `canvas`.
482	    func position(on canvas: CGSize) -> (x: Double, y: Double) {
483	        let y = canvas.height > canvas.width ? tallYFraction ?? yFraction : yFraction
484	        return (xFraction * Double(canvas.width), y * Double(canvas.height))
485	    }
486	
487	    /// Text ▸ Presets' two patches: the face, size, alignment and backdrop, and where the
488	    /// box sits at full opacity.
489	    func patches(on canvas: CGSize) -> (text: TextPatch, video: VideoPatch) {
490	        let at = position(on: canvas)
491	        return (
492	            TextPatch(
493	                font: font, size: size(on: canvas), align: align, valign: "middle",
494	                backdrop: .some(backdrop)),
495	            VideoPatch(x: at.x, y: at.y, opacity: 1)
496	        )
497	    }

518	// MARK: - Faces
519	
520	/// The model's one font string ↔ the panel's family + style pair.
521	///
522	/// Everything here tolerates a name this machine has no font for: a project
523	/// carries PostScript names, and the Text tab still has to open (and still has
524	/// to be able to change the face) on a machine missing that family.
525	enum TextFace {
526	    /// Installed families, sorted. Read once — `availableFontFamilies` walks
527	    /// the font registry, and this popup is rebuilt on every selection change.
528	    static let families: [String] = NSFontManager.shared.availableFontFamilies.sorted()
529	
530	    /// One member of a family: its PostScript name and the style label.
531	    struct Member {
532	        let name: String
533	        let style: String
534	    }
535	
536	    static func members(of family: String) -> [Member] {
537	        let raw = NSFontManager.shared.availableMembers(ofFontFamily: family) ?? []
538	        return raw.compactMap { entry in
539	            guard entry.count >= 2, let name = entry[0] as? String,
540	                  let style = entry[1] as? String
541	            else { return nil }
542	            return Member(name: name, style: style)
543	        }
544	    }
545	
546	    /// The family a stored PostScript name belongs to; the first installed
547	    /// family when the font is missing, so the popup always has a row.
548	    static func family(of postScriptName: String) -> String {
549	        if let font = NSFont(name: postScriptName, size: 12), let family = font.familyName {
550	            return family
551	        }
552	        return families.first ?? "Helvetica"
553	    }
554	
555	    /// The style label of a stored name ("SemiBold"), or "Regular".
556	    static func style(of postScriptName: String) -> String {
557	        let family = family(of: postScriptName)
558	        return members(of: family).first { $0.name == postScriptName }?.style ?? "Regular"
559	    }
560	
561	    /// The PostScript name for a family plus a style label, keeping the style
562	    /// across a family change when the new family has one by that name.
563	    static func postScriptName(family: String, style: String) -> String {
564	        let list = members(of: family)
565	        if let match = list.first(where: { $0.style == style }) { return match.name }
566	        if let regular = list.first(where: { $0.style == "Regular" }) { return regular.name }
567	        return list.first?.name ?? family
568	    }
569	}
